Article Title: 18,000 special trains, 700 AI cameras: Railways prepares for festive rush
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Union railway minister Ashwini Vaishnaw on Saturday said the Railways has deployed 18,000 special trains this festive season to manage the rush during Durga Puja, Diwali and Chhath, up from 12,000 operated last year.Vaishnaw said holding areas have been set up at around 20 railway stations to help passengers wait comfortably for their trains. Ticket counters have also been shifted from station premises to these areas, while additional scanning counters have been installed to speed up security checks and prevent long queues.The Railways has also installed around 700 AI-enabled cameras as part of its crowd-management measures, he said.“Special trains have been stationed at various locations, including Shakur Basti, Nizamuddin, Anand Vihar, Anand Vihar Terminal, and near New Delhi station,” Vaishnaw said.He added that the Railways operated around 75,000 special trains in the previous financial year, with the number expected to cross 80,000 this year.Referring to the situation on Chhoti Diwali, the minister said passenger movement and traffic at railway stations had returned to normal.“Even today, on the occasion of Chhoti Diwali, the traffic situation across all locations has already returned to normal. We intend to maintain this throughout the festive season,” he said.While speaking on train delays, network congestion, freight movement, and long-term capacity expansion projects, Vaishnaw said, "We are currently experiencing a period of peak congestion. There is a peak in the movement of coal and other goods. To address this, 36,000 kilometres of additional tracks have been laid over the last 10 years. Constructing new tracks and increasing capacity is crucial; this is the only way to provide a permanent solution. We must continue to build more tracks."
Article Summary: Railways has deployed 18,000 special trains this festive season to manage the rush during Durga Puja, Diwali and Chhath. Vaishnaw said holding areas have been set up at around 20 railway stations to help passengers wait comfortably for their trains.

NEW DELHI: Referring to the contradictory orders given by Supreme Court in the matter of bail to the accused on the ground of delay in trial and long incarceration for UAPA offences, which have been referred to a larger bench for authoritative pronouncement, former student activists Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam have moved SC for bail in 2020 Delhi riots cases.The accused submitted that two co-accused, including Tasleem Ahmed, were granted bail by SC on the grou-nd that determination of the issues by the larger bench would take time, and they could not be made to suffer continued incarceration.Seeking parity with the co-accused, Sharjeel Imam, who has already spent six years and nine months in custody, said in his petition, filed through advocate Fauzia Shakil, that two co-accused in the same FIR were released on interim bail by the court on May 22 under a principle which applies to him in greater degree.The accused moved SC after their plea for bail was rejected by the trial court and Delhi High Court on the ground that the apex court had purportedly set a deadline of Jan 5, 2027, for them to file a bail petition.The petition asked "whether the principle recognised by this Court in Tasleem Ahmed v. State order dated 22.05.2026, that an accused cannot be made to suffer continued incarceration merely because an important question of law has arisen for authoritative settlement, can be withheld from the petitioner alone by reference to the role attributed to him, when the question referred to concerns the correctness of the very judgment which declined his bail and relief in Tasleem Ahmed case was granted without any examination of role?"It further argued, "Whether liberty reserved by this Court in a judgment declining bail, to renew the prayer for bail at a defined point, operates as a bar upon the statutory jurisdiction of the Special Court and of the High Court to consider an application for bail founded on supervening circumstances be-fore that point, when the same paragraph of the judgment holds that pre-trial detention cannot be permitted to continue without regard to the progress of the trial and that Article 21 operates as a continuing check against continued incarceration without substantial progress of the trial?"
Article Summary: Former student activists Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam have moved SC for bail in 2020 Delhi riots cases. The accused submitted that two co-accused, including Tasleem Ahmed, were granted bail by SC on the grou-nd that determination of the issues by the larger bench would take time.

Article Title: Centre eases immigration rules for Pakistani, Afghan minorities and other foreign nationals
Article Text:
The order also streamlines travel and identification protocols for the citizens of Nepal and Bhutan.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Union home ministry has relaxed passport and visa requirements for several categories of foreign nationals residing in India, including Pakistani citizens who entered prior to December 31, 2009 with the intention to permanently reside in India but could not renew their Pakistani passport due to non-possession of computerised nationality identity card issued by Pakistan government.Other categories of foreign nationals for whom passport and visa rules have been eased as part of the Immigration and Foreigners (Exemption) (Amendment) ORder, 2026, include citizens of Pakistan, Afghanistan and Pakistan belonging to their religious minorities; Sri Lankan Tamil refugees and Tibetans.The order also streamlines travel and identification protocols for the citizens of Nepal and Bhutan, allowing them to enter or exit India by producing any one of the documents specified in the visa manual; However, in case they are entering or exiting India from or to a place other than Nepal or Bhutan, they must in possession of a valid passport. Nepal and Bhutan citizens who have embarked at or transited through China Macau, Hong Kong or Pakistan, must be in possession of both a valid passport and valid visa.The requirement of a valid passport and visa would also not apply to a male member of the Muslim community, being originally an Indian citizen, who went to Pakistan after partition between August 15, 1947 and Dec 31, 1965 leaving behind family in India and returned to India on or before Dec 31, 2009, and settled in Keralam on a valid Pakistani passport but which has since expired or been lost.However, such a person should not have married or acquired immoveable property while in Pakistan; ,while going to Pakistan, left behind family members who are Indian citizens; shall not return to Pakistan; and should not have any adverse report from the police or security agencies.A citizen of India entering into India from Nepal or Bhutan or departing from India to Nepal or Bhutan by land or air shall produce before the immigration officer one of the documents specified in the visa manual to establish their identity, though this exemption would not be applicable if departing to or returning from countries other than Nepal or Bhutan through the Indo-Nepal or Indo-Bhutan border of by air. In all such cases, a valid passport will be required and the exit and entry into India shall be only through the designated immigration points.The provisions in the Act and rules with regard to requirement of valid passport or other valid travel document and valid visa for entry into, stay in and exit from India, shall also not apply for a member of naval, military or air forces of India, entering into or exiting from India on duty and members of the family of any such person when accompanying him on a government transport; registered Sri Lankan Tamil nationals who have taken shelter in India up to Jan 9, 2015; as well as the foreign crew of foreign military vessels coming for repairs in India who are granted military ship repair permits by the immigration officer, provided they hold their military identification documents.Exempted categories include a Tibetan who has entered India after 1959 but before May 30,, 2003 on an entry permit issued by the Embassy of India in Kathmandu; or who entered after May 30, 2003, on the special entry permit issued through the designated immigration post on the Indo-Nepal border and a certificate of registration was issued by the registration officer concerned.Hindu, Sikh, Buddhist, Christian, Jain and Parsi citizens of Pakistan who entered India before Dec 31, 2024, fearing religious persecution in their home country, without valid documents including passport or other travel documents; or with valid documents including passport that has since expired, would also get relief under the amended Immigration and Foreigners (Exemption) order. However, such a person shall be required to obtain an appropriate category of visa after their entry into India, for continued stay.Also exempt now from requirement of a valid passport and visa are persons of Indian origin who subsequently acquired the citizenship of Malaysia or Singapore and returned to India on or before Dec 31, 2009 on a valid passport issued by either of those countries, which has since expired and is not being renewed by those countries because such person does not meet the conditions specified by those countries. Such persons must have documentary proof that they are a person of Indian origin.
Article Summary: The order also streamlines travel and identification protocols for the citizens of Nepal and Bhutan. Pakistani citizens who entered prior to December 31, 2009 could not renew their Pakistani passport due to non-possession of computerised nationality identity card. Other categories of foreign nationals for whom passport and visa rules have been eased include citizens of Pakistan, Afghanistan and Pakistan belonging to their religious minorities.

Article Title: Ousted Videocon promoter Dhoot declared bankrupt over dues worth Rs 12,668cr
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: From a Bajaj Auto dealership in Maharashtra to one of the largest consumer durable companies in the country, life has come full circle for Videocon Industries' ousted promoter Venugopal Dhoot who was declared bankrupt by National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) a day before Dhanteras, reports Amit Anand Choudhary.Dhoot is one of the most high-profile individuals to be declared bankrupt under the decade-old Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code , with the Mumbai bench of NCLT directing him to file his statement of financial position within seven days with the bankruptcy trustee Asish Narayan, who will manage his estate.A bench of judicial member Vinay Goel and technical member Charanjeet Singh Gulati declared Dhoot bankrupt over dues of Rs 12,668 crore, including interest and penalty, as he had given a personal guarantee for credit facilities extended to Videocon Industries and borrowings connected with Videocon Telecommunications. The petition was filed by State Bank of India."We are satisfied that the petition complies with all the requirements prescribed in Section 123 of the Code. Therefore, we consider it proper to admit this petition and pass the following orders: Venugopal Nandlal Dhoot, the personal guarantor herein, is declared as bankrupt," the tribunal said in its order.The bankruptcy trustee will issue a public notice inviting claims from creditors.The trustee will also handle administration and distribution of the estate.The development is bad news for promoters who had availed loans based on personal guarantees, a norm for corporate loans in the last three decades, but subsequently lost control over their companies as IBC was used for repeated defaults in repayment of dues.While provisions related to personal guarantors were notified in Dec 2019, till last June, close to 5,200 applications had been filed for initiation of personal insolvency of which 5,135 were filed with NCLT and the remaining 51 went to debt recovery tribunals. Of the 64 cases that have been approved, the repayment plans have yielded Rs 234 crore -- 1% of the admitted claims, official data showed.Unlike corporate insolvency, where a resolution professional is appointed by NCLT when the case is admitted and a resolution entity then takes over the company, in case of personal bankruptcies, the guarantor has to prepare a repayment plan, which needs to be approved by the tribunal.
Article Summary: Venugopal Dhoot is one of the most high-profile individuals to be declared bankrupt under the decade-old Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code. The Mumbai bench of NCLT directed him to file his statement of financial position within seven days with the bankruptcy trustee Asish Narayan.

NEW DELHI: Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) Friday released date sheets for the Class X and XII board examinations for 2027, with both scheduled to begin on Feb 16.The schedules were announced 101 days before the start of the examinations, giving students more than three months to prepare.According to a circular issued by CBSE controller of examinations Sanyam Bhardwaj, over 46.3 lakh students have registered for the 2027 examinations - more than 26.5 lakh from Class X and over 19.8 lakh from Class XII. While Class X students will appear in 83 subjects, Class XII students will take examinations in 121 subjects.All examinations will begin at 10.30 am.CBSE said the date sheets were finalised after the completion of the list of candidates submission process by schools and an analysis of the subject combinations opted for by students.Explaining the scheduling process, the board said, "More than 40,000 subject combinations have been factored in while preparing the date sheets to ensure that examinations of any two subjects opted by a student do not coincide on the same date."It said adequate gaps had been provided between examinations of subjects commonly offered together in both classes. It added that the tentative schedules of major entrance tests for Class XII students were also taken into account, with efforts made to conclude the boards before the entrance tests.
Article Summary: The schedules were announced 101 days before the start of the examinations, giving students more than three months to prepare. Over 46.3 lakh students have registered for the 2027 examinations. While Class X students will appear in 83 subjects, Class XII students will take examinations in 121 subjects.

Article Title: HC judge vacancies at decade-low 26%, but pendency keeps piling up
Article Text:
Allahabad High Court

With 64 lakh cases, backlog refuses to ease

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: After hovering between 36% and 40% over the past decade, vacancies in HC judges have shown a significant decline, falling to 26%, this despite sanctioned strength of judges in HCs increasing from 906 in 2014 to 1,122.The largest HC, Allahabad, has brought down its vacancies to 56 against a sanctioned strength of 160 judges, as of Nov 1.The other HCs with bigger benches and usually large vacancies - Bombay, Punjab and Haryana, Madras, Calcutta, Karnataka and Delhi - too, have increased their working strength, bringing down vacancies.The last time judges' vacancies were this low (at 26%) was in July 2009, when there were 234 judges posts to be filled against a sanctioned strength of 886 in 21 HCs then.Vacancies in HCs started gradually climbing thereafter, which coincided with the friction between higher judiciary and govt over an attempt to bring a judicial accountability bill and passage of National Judicial Appointments Commission Act by Parliament. NJAC Act was later struck down by Supreme Court.In Nov 2014, vacancies were at 36% (in 24 HCs), with 353 judges posts vacant against a sanctioned strength of 984.These vacancies remained at 35% in March 2022 with 387 posts vacant, though the sanctioned strength was increased to 1,104 judges.Large vacancies are a prime factor behind backlog of cases. Though SC historically never had large vacancies, case pendency in SC has increased from 52,000 in 2009 to more than 92,000 at present.The situation is worse in HCs and much worse in district and lower judiciary, deteriorating every month. In 2009, total pendency of cases in HCs was at 39.5 lakh, which climbed to 45 lakh in 2013, and is at 64 lakh at present.The pendency in lower judiciary is similarly getting worse while the large number of vacancies remain static at around 5,000 against a sanctioned strength of 25,894 judicial officers.
Article Summary: Vacancies in HC judges have shown a significant decline, falling to 26%. This despite sanctioned strength of judges in HCs increasing from 906 in 2014 to 1,122. The last time judges' vacancies were this low (at 26%) was in July 2009.

Article Title: NMC adds 9,783 PG medical seats, takes total to 68,305
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: India's postgraduate medical education system is set for a major expansion, with 9,783 seats being added for the 2026-27 academic year. The increase takes the total approved PG intake to 68,305, up from 58,522, with govt medical colleges accounting for the largest share of the new seats.Of the additional seats, 4,373 have been added in govt colleges, 4,148 in private colleges and 1,262 in deemed universities, Dr M K Ramesh, president of NMC's Medical Assessment and Rating Board (MARB), told TOI.PG medical seats are spread across several states, with five accounting for a little over half of the national intake. Karnataka has the highest number, with 8,998 approved seats for 2026-27, followed by Maharashtra with 7,682. Uttar Pradesh has 6,983 seats, Tamil Nadu 6,819 and Telangana 4,417. Together, these five states account for 34,899 seats, or around 51% of the total.
Article Summary: India's postgraduate medical education system is set for a major expansion. 9,783 seats are being added for the 2026-27 academic year. The increase takes the total approved PG intake to 68,305, up from 58,522. Karnataka has the highest number, with 8,998 approved seats.

Article Title: India’s only floating post office gets longer working hours
Article Text:
Dal Lake floating post office

SRINAGAR: Working hours at India’s only Floating Post Office, operating from a houseboat on Dal Lake in Srinagar, have been extended from five hours to 12 hours, Department of Posts announced Friday. According to the revised timings, the post office (PO) at Nehru Park will now remain open from 9am to 9pm.The move follows increased footfall and public demand for postal services beyond regular office hours, chief postmaster general, Jammu, Kashmir and Ladakh, Col Sagar Hanuman Singh said during a visit to the facility. He reviewed arrangements and interacted with locals and tourists.Col Singh said the initiative aims to provide greater convenience to customers. The extended hours will provide locals, houseboat operators, and tourists greater flexibility to access postal services, officials said.In 1953, the PO operated from a simple postal boat, catering to communities living on Dal Lake. It served as a vital link between the houseboats and the city. In 2011, the facility was officially renamed the Floating Post Office—an idea John Samuel, then-postmaster general of the J&K circle, introduced.The PO has a unique museum of rare stamps and postcards that portray the history of the postal service in J&K. Over time, it has become a popular tourist attraction.
Article Summary: India's only Floating Post Office, operating from a houseboat on Dal Lake in Srinagar, has been extended from five hours to 12 hours. The extended hours will provide locals, houseboat operators, and tourists greater flexibility to access postal services, officials said.

Article Title: ‘Experimenting on 1.3 billion people’: Priyank Kharge alleges excess ethanol blending in E20 petrol
Article Text:
Representative image

Rahul Gandhi questions E20 petrol content; oil companies dispute Karnataka findings

Kharge questions Centre's stand on ethanol blending

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Karnataka minister Priyank Kharge on Saturday accused the Central government of misleading people over ethanol blending in petrol, alleging that reports from government-accredited laboratories showed ethanol content exceeding the limits announced by the Centre.Kharge also alleged that the ethanol-blending programme was being used to benefit companies linked to the families of Union ministers. He claimed that some laboratory reports had indicated blending levels of up to 35-40 per cent, while others showed 31 per cent."The Government of India is lying through its teeth to the people. Very clearly, they had said that it (ethanol) will not be blended beyond a certain capacity, but NABL reports have proved that the ethanol blending is crossing the permissible limits, or at least the set limits that the govt had proclaimed. It's up to 35%, 40% in some cases. The lab reports are endorsed by laboratories that are accredited by the Govt of India," he said, as quoted by news agency ANI.The minister alleged that the policy was intended to facilitate certain companies. "This entire ethanol blending has been done only to facilitate companies of Union ministers," he said.Kharge's remarks came after Congress leader Rahul Gandhi accused the Centre of failing to disclose the actual ethanol content in petrol being sold across the country.In a post on X, the Congress MP said tests conducted on petrol samples collected from seven districts in Karnataka had found ethanol levels above the prescribed 20 per cent.He claimed that 11 of the 14 samples tested contained more than 20 per cent ethanol, with samples from Indian Oil Corporation (IOCL) and Hindustan Petroleum Corporation (HPCL) recording 31.2 per cent and 30.5 per cent, respectively.Karnataka food, civil supplies, consumer affairs and legal metrology minister Rizwan Arshad had said the samples were collected from Bengaluru, Kolar, Chikkaballapura, Bengaluru Rural, Ramanagara, Mangaluru and Tumakuru. The tests were conducted by the NABL-accredited and ISO-certified Shriram Research Institute in Bengaluru.However, state-run oil marketing companies IOC, BPCL and HPCL have disputed the Karnataka government's findings. In a joint statement, the companies said E20 petrol supplied across their retail networks, including in Karnataka, complied with the Bureau of Indian Standards' IS 17021 specifications, which prescribe an ethanol content of 19-21 per cent.The companies also questioned the sampling and testing procedures used by the state government, saying the third-party laboratory certificates did not provide sufficient details of the testing methodology to independently verify the reported levels.Kharge referred to the Solicitor General's submission before the Supreme Court, in which ethanol blending was described as an experiment that was not being implemented across the country."If you recollect, the Solicitor General had told in the Supreme Court that this entire ethanol blending was an experiment and is not happening throughout the country, but if you actually look closely, you are experimenting on 1.3 billion people. How does that even work? So it is very clear that this Government of India has been lying to its own people only for profiteering," he said.He also cited the 31 per cent blending figure and referred to concerns raised by vehicle manufacturers over possible damage to vehicles."This is cheating the public, cheating being done for the company of a central minister's son. What is the NABL organisation saying? 31% blending is happening. They themselves are saying. Vehicle organisations have written letters saying vehicles are getting damaged; they have also threatened and intimidated, and got it withdrawn. Yesterday Rizwan Arshad spoke about NABL, where are BJP people now?" Kharge said.Rahul has also claimed that excessive ethanol blending could affect vehicle performance, leading to lower mileage and higher maintenance costs. He questioned the absence of labels at fuel stations disclosing the ethanol content of petrol.India's ethanol-blending programme began with a pilot initiative in 2001 and aims to reduce dependence on imported crude oil, strengthen domestic agricultural value chains and improve energy security.According to petroleum ministry data cited by the oil marketing companies, the programme has generated foreign exchange savings of more than Rs 1.97 lakh crore since the 2014-15 ethanol supply year, substituted around 316 lakh metric tonnes of crude oil and reduced carbon dioxide emissions by approximately 952 lakh metric tonnes.During the 2025-26 ethanol supply year, which ended on October 31, 2026, the three public sector oil marketing companies procured 1,089 crore litres of ethanol and blended 1,134 crore litres against petrol sales of around 5,673 crore litres.
Article Summary: Karnataka minister Priyank Kharge accused the Central government of misleading people over ethanol blending in petrol. Kharge also alleged that the ethanol- blending programme was being used to benefit companies linked to the families of Union ministers. Congress leader Rahul Gandhi accused the Centre of failing to disclose the actual ethanol content in petrol being sold across the country.

Article Title: Cancer in India: Screening exists, but why are patients still diagnosed late
Article Text:
Offered, not taken: Why India still finds cancer late

A public programme that exists, and a habit that has not formed

What the national survey found

Why cancers are found late

Who should be screened, and when

Vaccination and cervical cancer

The barrier he names: Awareness

The urban and rural gap

The case for a yearly check-up

What it will take

Cancer in India is often detected late. By the time many patients are diagnosed, the disease has already advanced, when treatment is harder and the chances of survival are lower. Part of the explanation lies in how screening is organised in the country, and part lies in how people respond to early warning signs.The stakes are considerable. The Indian Council of Medical Research’s National Cancer Registry Programme estimated 13.92 lakh new cancer cases in India in 2020, up from 13.25 lakh in 2018, and about 7.7 lakh cancer deaths in 2020, according to figures the Union Health Ministry placed before Lok Sabha. The question that follows is how many of these cases could have been caught sooner.India does run a public screening system. The National Programme for Prevention and Control of Cancer, Diabetes, Cardiovascular Diseases and Stroke, now called the National Programme for Prevention and Control of Non-Communicable Diseases (NP-NCD), was launched in 2010 in 100 districts across 21 states. In 2016, population-based screening was added for everyone aged 30 and above. It covers hypertension, diabetes and three cancers: of the oral cavity, the cervix and the breast.The design is meant to bring screening close to the community. Under the Health Ministry’s guidelines, an ASHA worker completes a Community Based Assessment Checklist. People aged 30 to 65 are then offered an oral visual examination and, for women, a clinical breast examination and a visual inspection of the cervix with acetic acid.Each is meant to be repeated once in five years. The ministry’s training module for staff nurses estimates that in a population of 1,000, about 370 people are eligible for oral cancer screening and about 182 women each for breast and cervical screening. The cervical test is offered at the primary health centre level to begin with.Uptake is low. The fifth National Family Health Survey, conducted between 2019 and 2021, asked adults aged 30 to 49 whether they had ever been screened for cancer. Among women, 1.9 per cent reported ever having had a cervical cancer screening test, 0.9 per cent a breast examination and 0.9 per cent an oral cavity examination. Among men, 1.2 per cent reported ever having had an oral cancer examination.The variation between states was wide. Tamil Nadu recorded the highest rates for cervical and breast screening, at 9.8 per cent and 5.6 per cent respectively. Cervical screening stood at 0.2 per cent in Gujarat, Assam and West Bengal, and in at least half of the states and Union Territories fewer than one per cent of women had ever been screened for it.Dr Prasad’s explanation has two parts. India has no mandatory screening programme, he said, and patients often ignore early signs, so they are diagnosed only when the disease is at an advanced stage.The Health Ministry’s 2016 operational framework for cancer screening makes the same point about late detection. It says cancers in India tend to be detected late, leaving little room for effective treatment, and cites five-year survival of 60.2, 76.3 and 73.2 per cent for early-stage oral, breast and cervical cancers, against 3.3, 14.9 and 7.9 per cent at an advanced stage. The figures come from a 2010 population-based study.The framework also stresses that screening is not an end in itself. It needs assured treatment, regular follow-up and linkages between every level of care, so that a person who tests positive can reach confirmation and treatment.Dr Prasad’s recommendations differ from what the public programme offers, and he set them out group by group.As per the guidelines, Dr Prasad said, women should begin breast cancer screening at 40. Women who are sexually active should be tested from 21, mainly to prevent cervical cancer. Men between 45 and 50 can have a Prostate Specific Antigen test once a year. Men and women alike should have a colonoscopy once every 10 years from the age of 50. From 40, he said, both men and women should mandatorily undergo a master health screening.The two differ in scope, age and frequency. The national framework’s screening protocols cover three cancers, oral, breast and cervical, for people aged 30 to 65, at five-year intervals; prostate and colorectal cancers are not among them. The framework itself notes that breast screening yields much more in women over 40, but keeps the starting age at 30 for programmatic and operational reasons.Dr Prasad also pointed to vaccination against cervical cancer for girls aged 9 to 14, which he said can prevent cervical cancer in women by up to 95 to 98 per cent. The Union Budget speech of February 2024 had announced that the government would encourage vaccination for girls in that age group.The national HPV vaccination campaign was launched in February 2026. It offers a free, voluntary, single-dose vaccine to 14-year-old girls, with parental consent, at government health facilities. The Health Ministry puts the annual cohort of 14-year-olds at about 1.2 crore girls, citing Registrar General of India estimates.By 11 September 2026, more than 80 lakh doses had been administered, the ministry said. Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh and Mizoram reported 100 per cent coverage of their identified target groups, while Bihar, Andhra Pradesh and Assam had crossed 90 per cent. Uttar Pradesh had vaccinated more than 22 lakh girls, the highest of any state.Asked whether cost, fear, lack of awareness or access keeps people from being screened, Dr Prasad said it is mainly lack of awareness, along with the belief that nothing will happen to them. “Anything can happen to anyone at any point of time,” he said.The Health Ministry’s 2016 framework makes a related point. Because awareness of health is low, it says, screening for conditions with no obvious symptoms is seen as unnecessary, particularly among the poor, for whom a day’s visit to a secondary or tertiary facility can mean a lost day’s wages. On the cost of treatment, the Health Ministry has told Parliament that care in government hospitals is either free or highly subsidised for the poor and needy.In cities, Dr Prasad said, access and availability are plentiful, and a person with symptoms can reach cancer care. In tier two and tier three cities the best cancer care may not be available, he said, but screening is available in almost all government colleges and hospitals. Where tier one cities hold a clear advantage is awareness, because their residents have easier access to information about screening.The public cancer care network is meant to narrow the rest of the distance. Under the central government’s scheme for strengthening tertiary care for cancer, 19 State Cancer Institutes and 20 Tertiary Care Cancer Centres have been approved. The Centre and states share the cost in a 60:40 ratio, and 90:10 for the North-Eastern and hilly states, according to a reply in Rajya Sabha. In the Union Budget for 2025-26, the Finance Minister said the government would facilitate day-care cancer centres in all district hospitals over three years, with 200 to be set up in 2025-26.Asked for the one change that would do the most, Dr Prasad proposed mandatory health check-ups, once a year or at least once in two years, for everyone working in the government and private sectors.He expects the benefit to travel beyond the employee. This should also help in getting family members checked, he said, as many of them will come forward for testing. Cancer screening under the national programme, by comparison, is meant to be repeated once in five years.The pieces are not missing. A public programme offers screening for three cancers to people aged 30 to 65. A vaccination campaign is reaching 14-year-old girls through government facilities, and the Budget has announced day-care cancer centres for district hospitals. What the 2019–21 survey shows is a gap between what is offered and what people take up, with fewer than two in every hundred women aged 30 to 49 having ever been screened for cervical cancer.Dr Prasad’s account of that gap is a simple one: people do not think it can happen to them.
Article Summary: Cancer in India is often detected late, leaving little room for effective treatment. India has no mandatory screening programme, and patients often ignore early signs. Tamil Nadu recorded the highest rates for cervical and breast screening. Cervical screening stood at 0.2 per cent in Gujarat, Assam and West Bengal.

Article Text:

NEW DELHI: In a major crackdown on drug production, the Narcotics Control Bureau’s Itanagar Zonal Unit, operating alongside the Sashastra Seema Bal, Central Reserve Police Force, and Arunachal Pradesh Police, has eradicated approximately 458 acres of illicit cannabis cultivation in the Kalaktang subdivision of West Kameng district.The first phase of the joint destruction operation, carried out between October 26 and November 3, 2026, resulted in the destruction of over 1.37 lakh kilograms of cannabis plants grown primarily on community lands.The drive mobilized 118 personnel and workers, drawing enforcement officers from the Sashastra Seema Bal, Central Reserve Police Force, Arunachal Pradesh Anti-Narcotics Task Force, West Kameng Police, and the district administration. NEW DELHI: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) has initiated an investigation against two foreign entities for their alleged involvement in India's domestic affairs and in connection with a suspicious transfer of $1 million to a UK-based firm having links to India.ED has identified TCC Digital Markets Ltd, a firm registered in the tax haven of Saint Kitts and Nevis, as the source of funds that reached entities and individuals in India through layered transactions, moving across different jurisdictions, including Germany, Dubai, Lithuania, Canada, St Kitts and the UK.Dr Matthias Karl Vogt Trust of Germany has been identified as the actual source of the $1 million fund, which was transferred to a UK-based entity through layered transactions before being moved to India.The German trust had first transferred the funds to XBase Digital UAB (Lithuania) to get around German law, according to a senior official aware of the probe.Initial probe led the agency to an undated letter from Dr Matthias Vogt, which stated that the payment was made in digital currency.Intelligence gathered by the agency revealed that digital assets were suspected to have come from 'hawala' (illegal money transfers) to Dubai and to the Lithuanian entity, before they were moved to the UK.The UK-based firm, recipient of Vogt's money, received $1 million between Feb and March 2026 in its Airwallex (UK) Ltd account. The money passed through multiple layers of different channels and entities, including one registered in Lithuania.Also read: SC to NewsClick: Reply to ED plea against HC order quashing ECIR It finally took the form of a "grant" from the Saint Kitts and Nevis islands-registered firm, which transferred the funds in two tranches of GB,67,006 and GB,71,746 to the UK firm, before they reached end users in India, sources familiar with the investigation said.The Caribbean islands are known as a tax haven convenient for laundering proceeds of crime by global economic offenders.The enforcement agency has come across another transaction by a Canadian-registered entity, ZBase Digital Inc, which had transferred $500,000 in Feb to the same UK firm's Airwallex account. Article Title: Creamy layer verdict only for those who challenged government decision, says SC
Article Text:
.

Order won't be ground to reopen appointments already made: SC

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Friday said its March 2026 verdict quashing Centre's 2004 decision to factor in salary income of PSU and private sector employees for deciding creamy layer status for OBCs would be applicable only to those who had moved the court, while those already appointed and allotted cadre would not be disturbed.The clarification came following apprehension in many quarters that the March order would affect all subsequent appointments as those denied reservation in the last decades on that calculation would become eligible for fresh entry into the civil services.In March, SC had held that income of parents could not be the sole criterion to determine whether a candidate fell in the creamy layer for exclusion from OBC reservation and the status and category of parents' job had to be considered along with 'income/wealth test' as an additional criterion of exclusion.The ruling has huge implications for wards of PSU and private sector employees as in their case, parents' income was taken as the sole factor to determine creamy layer status, unlike in the case of govt job employees whose category of job was the deciding factor. As it created uncertainty over the validity of the recruitment process for OBC candidates over the years, Centre sought clarification from Supreme Court, saying its order should not be enforced retrospectively.The bench said, "The judgement determines the rights of the parties before this court. It holds that the respondent candidates fall within the non-creamy layer of the OBC category and are entitled to the benefit of reservation together with consequential placement and allotment of posts in the selection processes in which they participated. The grant of such benefit shall not, by itself, operate to the detriment of the seniority of any other person or entail the reopening of selections or appointments already concluded. "Advocates Shashank Ratnoo and Varun Thakur, who represented the candidates who have been fighting a legal battle for years, said govt has to create supernumerary posts to accommodate their clients who fulfil the requisite eligibility conditions.The Supreme Court said its judgement shall not, by itself, furnish a ground for reopening selections or appointments already concluded prior to the order and the claims of those asserting that they are similarly placed and whose cases are pending before any court, tribunal or other competent forum or authority, may be considered on their own merits."This court expresses no opinion on the merits of such claims, save to reiterate that the interpretation of the 1993 OM and the 2004 letter laid down in the judgement may be taken into consideration while adjudicating such claims in accordance with law," the bench said.The office memorandum (OM) issued by Centre in 1993 had said the same principle would be applied to employees of PSUs, banks, insurance organisations, universities and similar bodies holding equivalent or comparable posts. But the "equivalence of posts" as contemplated in the OM was not done and a clarificatory letter was issued by govt in 2004 making 'income/wealth test' the sole criterion for PSUs and private sector employees.The court, however, had said overemphasis on the 2004 letter to the extent of making income alone determinative without regard to parental status or category of service would defeat the structural framework of exclusion envisaged under the 1993 office memorandum and there could not be different criteria for children of govt employees and the rest.
Article Summary: Supreme Court quashes Centre's 2004 decision to factor in salary income of PSU and private sector employees for deciding creamy layer status for OBCs. clarification came following apprehension in many quarters that the March order would affect all subsequent appointments as those denied reservation in the last decades on that calculation would become eligible for fresh entry into the civil services.

Article Title: Living near a highway toll plaza? New FASTag rule offers annual pass of up to Rs 3,000, but there's a catch
Article Text:
​The new annual local pass are available at eligible toll plazas since Nov 1. Motorists will also be able to obtain it through the Rajmargyatra app from Dec 1

The need for FASTag: India's highway boom and the push for seamless travel

India's highway network rapidly grew over the years; so did FASTag

The challenges: What FASTag solved, and what it couldn't

What changes: New FASTag rules, cheaper local passes and the catch

Eligibility for the annual local pass.

Why living within 20 km may not be enough

When can motorists obtain the pass, and how is it different from the FASTag Annual Pass?

The future: From FASTag to satellite-based toll collection

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Living within 20 km of a National Highway toll plaza could now mean lower toll expenses for motorists. From November 1, 2026, eligible owners of non-commercial vehicles can obtain a Concessional Local Pass for an annual fee of Rs 1,500 at toll plazas outside municipal or local town limits, and Rs 3,000 at those within these limits, according to the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways.But simply living nearby does not guarantee eligibility. The scheme requires motorists to have a valid and functional FASTag , restricts the pass to a specific toll plaza and excludes highways and expressways operating under a closed user-fee collection system. It also rules out issuance where a service road or alternative road is available to commuters.The concession comes as India continues to expand its highway network and transition towards electronic toll collection . While FASTag has reduced dependence on cash payments and cut waiting times at toll plazas, operational challenges persist, prompting the government to introduce further changes to the system.India's National Highway network has expanded significantly over the past decade, making efficient toll collection increasingly important. The network grew from 91,287 km in financial year 2013-14 to 1,46,572 km in March 2026, according to an infrastructure factsheet released by the Press Information Bureau (PIB) in August 2026.As highways and expressways multiply, ensuring uninterrupted traffic movement has become critical.Long queues at toll plazas can undermine the very benefits that faster road infrastructure is meant to deliver, particularly during peak travel periods.Before electronic toll collection became widespread, motorists had to stop at toll booths and pay manually. This often meant long delays, higher fuel consumption from idling vehicles and increased pollution. Cash handling also made toll collection more dependent on physical transactions and records.The government introduced electronic toll collection to address these bottlenecks.FASTag uses Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) technology. A tag affixed to a vehicle's windscreen communicates with electronic readers at toll plazas, enabling the applicable fee to be deducted from the linked account without requiring motorists to pay cash at the booth. The ministry documented the launch of electronic toll collection on the Delhi-Mumbai corridor on October 31, 2014, describing FASTag as a passive RFID tag.The system was subsequently rolled out across National Highways. From midnight on February 15-16, 2021, all lanes at National Highway fee plazas were designated as FASTag lanes, according to the ministry's year-end review.Adoption has grown substantially since then. In its October 27, 2026 announcement on the new local pass, the ministry said more than 13 crore FASTags had been issued across the country. A separate Rajya Sabha reply dated July 22, 2026, stated that approximately 98% of National Highway user-fee collection was being carried out through FASTag.The transition has created a digital trail of toll transactions, reduced dependence on cash collection and improved transparency and accounting in the process.FASTag addressed several problems associated with conventional toll collection, particularly queues and delays caused by cash transactions. Automatic deductions helped reduce the time vehicles spent at toll booths.Road Transport Minister Nitin Gadkari said in June 2023 that waiting time at toll plazas had fallen from 734 seconds in 2014 to 47 seconds in 2023 following the introduction of electronic toll collection.However, digitising payments has not eliminated operational problems. Motorists continue to encounter issues involving FASTag activation, insufficient account balance, damaged or improperly affixed tags and failed transactions.In January 2026, the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) announced changes to the Know Your Vehicle (KYV) process for car-category FASTags, acknowledging that post-activation verification requirements had caused inconvenience and delays. The authority also cited complaints involving loosely affixed tags, incorrect issuance and misuse.Disputes over incorrect deductions have also necessitated dedicated grievance-redressal mechanisms. A July 2026 parliamentary reply listed the National Highway helpline 1033, issuer-bank helplines, the Rajmargyatra app and a dedicated email address as channels through which motorists can lodge complaints.Another persistent concern involves residents living close to National Highway toll plazas. Even as FASTag has made toll collection quicker, people who regularly cross a nearby plaza on short journeys continue to face recurring toll expenses.The existing monthly local-pass arrangement was designed to address this problem. In August 2026, NHAI announced that online subscriptions for monthly local passes had been extended to 121 toll plazas through the Rajmargyatra app. The new annual concession builds on this facility, offering eligible residents another option.The government has introduced the Concessional Local Pass for eligible owners of non-commercial vehicles residing within 20 km of a National Highway fee plaza. The provision was notified through the National Highways Fee (Determination of Rates and Collection) (Fifth Amendment) Rules, 2026, under the National Highways Act, 1956.According to the ministry's October 27 announcement, the scheme came into effect on November 1, 2026, with two annual fee structures depending on the location of the toll plaza.Motorists using fee plazas outside municipal or local town limits will have to pay Rs 1,500 annually. For plazas located within these limits, the annual fee has been fixed at Rs 3,000.To qualify, applicants must own an eligible non-commercial vehicle, reside within the specified 20-km radius and possess a valid and functional FASTag. Commercial vehicles are excluded.Eligible motorists can choose between the existing monthly local pass and the new concessional annual pass. However, the annual pass is valid only at the specific toll plaza for which it is issued. It cannot be used at other plazas along the same highway or elsewhere on the National Highway network.The new rules contain additional exclusions that could deny eligibility even to residents who meet the distance requirement.The first applies to National Highways and expressways where toll collection operates under a closed user-fee collection system. The ministry has clarified that the concessional local pass will not be available on these stretches.The second exclusion concerns toll plazas where a service road or alternative road is available for commuters. According to the ministry's announcement, the annual local pass will not be issued in such cases.In other words, residential proximity alone is not enough. The toll collection system in operation and the availability of alternative roads will also determine eligibility. However, the PIB announcement does not spell out how authorities will assess the availability of alternative roads or resolve disputes involving residential distances and municipal boundaries.The pass is also restricted to the designated toll plaza and cannot be used at other locations. The government has retained the power to revise the annual rates, with any revisions taking effect from April 1 each year.The ministry has said that the new annual local pass will be available at eligible toll plazas from November 1, 2026. Motorists will also be able to obtain it through the Rajmargyatra app from December 1, 2026.The new concession should not be confused with the separate FASTag Annual Pass introduced in August 2025. The latter is available to non-commercial cars, jeeps and vans and follows a different fee structure and coverage arrangement.For financial year 2026-27, the FASTag Annual Pass costs Rs 3,075 and remains valid for one year or 200 fee-plaza crossings, whichever comes first. It covers approximately 1,150 National Highway and National Expressway fee plazas, according to NHAI's rate-revision announcement.The distinction is important. While the FASTag Annual Pass offers wider geographical coverage, subject to a limit on crossings, the new Concessional Local Pass is meant specifically for residents living within 20 km of an eligible toll plaza and can be used only at that location.The actual savings under the new scheme will depend on the existing monthly-pass rate at the particular toll plaza and how frequently a motorist uses it. The two annual-pass arrangements therefore serve different purposes and should be assessed separately.Even as FASTag remains the backbone of electronic toll collection on National Highways, the government is exploring technologies that could eventually allow motorists to be charged according to the distance they travel.One such technology is the Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS)-based toll collection system. It uses satellite-based positioning to determine a vehicle's location and track its movement along designated highways. The applicable user fee can then be calculated according to the distance travelled, rather than relying solely on vehicles passing through conventional toll plazas.This is fundamentally different from FASTag, which primarily relies on RFID communication between a vehicle-mounted tag and electronic readers at tolling points. GNSS-based tolling could eventually enable distance-based charging and reduce the need for physical toll barriers.However, satellite-based toll collection has not replaced FASTag in India. In a July 2026 reply to the Rajya Sabha, the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways said expert committees had recommended further deliberations on GPS-based barrier-free tolling, citing concerns over security, privacy, data breaches and operational control. The response did not specify a nationwide implementation timeline.Meanwhile, the government is advancing Multi-Lane Free Flow (MLFF) toll collection, which allows vehicles to pass through tolling points without stopping at conventional barriers. Unlike GNSS-based tolling, MLFF can continue to use existing FASTag technology.The system combines Automatic Number Plate Recognition (ANPR) cameras, artificial intelligence-based analytics and FASTag-enabled RFID technology to identify vehicles and collect the applicable toll.The two technologies represent different approaches to seamless toll collection. MLFF aims to eliminate the need to stop at toll barriers while retaining electronic identification and payment mechanisms such as FASTag. GNSS-based tolling, on the other hand, could eventually make distance travelled the basis for calculating toll charges.For now, FASTag remains central to India's electronic toll collection network, even as the government experiments with barrier-free systems and explores satellite-based alternatives. The new concessional local pass adds another option for residents living near toll plazas, but its restrictions mean that not everyone within the 20-km radius will necessarily benefit.
Article Summary: The new annual local pass are available at eligible toll plazas since Nov 1. Motorists will also be able to obtain it through the Rajmargyatra app from Dec 1. The scheme requires motorists to have a valid and functional FASTag. It restricts the pass to a specific toll plaza and excludes highways and expressways under closed user-fee collection system.

Article Title: The watchman and the log scale
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

At IIT Delhi this week, the investor Gaurav Dalmia gave students twelve stories about how wealth gets made. The one that stays with you is about how easily it could have gone to someone else.Some years ago, Rajiv Bajaj was in Sikar, Rajasthan, in his great-grandfather's village, filming a documentary about his family. In the crowd he noticed a familiar face: a watchman from Bajaj Auto. Bajaj asked what he was doing there. The man said that this was home. His family and the Bajajs had been neighbours.The two families' fortunes parted over one decision. In 1894, a wealthy merchant named Seth Bachhraj adopted a small boy from the area, Jamnalal, to raise as his grandson and heir. Bajaj, telling the story later, thanked his luck, and wondered what would have followed had the merchant chosen the boy next door. The watchman's family might be running the company. Rajiv Bajaj might be the one on duty outside.Gaurav Dalmia told this story on Wednesday evening to the Economics and Finance Club at IIT Delhi. He placed it at the end of his first case study, almost as an aside. A room of students hoping to make their fortunes could be forgiven for hearing a charming digression. I think it was the most serious thing he said.Dalmia chairs Dalmia Group Holdings, which invests in private equity, property and public markets.I know him as a man who reads constantly and would rather talk about what he has read than about what he owns. His title for the evening could not have been drier: "Indian Business Landscape: Select Case Studies." There were twelve companies, most of them Indian, and most came with the same kind of chart, drawn on a log scale.A log scale is an unromantic thing. Each equal step up the page means the number has multiplied by the same amount, so a rise from 1 to 2 takes up as much room as a rise from 1,000 to 2,000. The drama of any given year shrinks. What remains is the rate of growth, held over decades. Look at enough of these charts and you begin to see business the way Dalmia seems to: slowly, and in ratios.He began with a man being wrong. In 1991, India's foreign reserves had fallen to about $1 billion, barely two or three weeks of imports, and the country opened up because it had little choice. Rahul Bajaj and the so-called Bombay Club asked for a gradual shift, fearing that Indian companies would be crushed before they could adapt. Dalmia's verdict took one sentence: Bajaj was wrong. Since 2002 alone, Bajaj Auto's revenue has grown almost 16-fold and its market value about 50-fold, or roughly 100-fold counting the spun-off Bajaj Finserv. The company whose patriarch feared foreign competition now sells in a hundred countries.Then came the long stretches when nothing seems to pay. Nvidia, today worth some $5 trillion, is now spoken of as destiny. By Dalmia's count, between 2004 and 2008 its profits rose more than 16-fold while its market value rose only 3.6 times, and in one year profits jumped 82 per cent while the stock did not move. Such years, he noted, weigh on a chief executive. Infosys , whose market value has gone from Rs 191 crore in 1994 to more than Rs 5 lakh crore, makes a related point: private equity firms often sell at listing, assuming the best years are over, and the people who buy from them often find that the party has just begun.Berkshire Hathaway supplied the arithmetic. A thousand dollars in 1965, compounding at the S&P 500's 10.6 per cent with dividends, became about $455,000. In Warren Buffett's company, at 19.8 per cent, it became nearly $61 million. You would hardly have noticed the gap in the first five years. And from 2020 to 2025, in the age of the technology stock, Berkshire beat the Nasdaq, 2.2 times to 1.8. "Many techies will find this very humbling," he told a room at an IIT.His second habit is a distrust of categories. Lakshmi Mittal, short of capital in his early years, bought the failing steel mills that bigger companies would not touch, the "hairy assets," at less than it would cost to build them new, starting with a loss-making plant in Trinidad and Tobago. His fortune went from $1.5 billion in 1996 to $45 billion in 2008. Varun Beverages, the Pepsi bottler, was Dalmia's example of how an old Western business can be a young Indian one. If wages are growing 9 to 11 per cent a year, he argued, then what millions of Indians have left after roti, kapda aur makaan is growing at 20 per cent or more. Fizzy drinks follow. Varun's annual profit went from Rs 42 crore in 2016 to more than Rs 3,000 crore.Cement is a dull commodity, unless you are Aliko Dangote in Nigeria, where poor infrastructure keeps competition out and a tonne earns about $24 in profit, against about $6 for India's UltraTech. A car company is a low-margin grind, unless you are Ferrari, which holds production to about 14,000 cars and barely advertises. Its revenue is about $8 billion, against Volkswagen's $364 billion. Its market value is larger than Volkswagen's. An industry, in Dalmia's telling, is an average, and averages hide the interesting people.The third thing he looks for is harder to chart. Dalmia invested early in the lender Incred in 2017, so he is hardly neutral about it, and he says that what drew him was the absence of a certain quality. Non-bank lending was then the flavour of the month. Plenty of founders were raising money on the trend with little of their own at stake, a free bet on someone else's capital. He calls this "bubble bravery," and it is a phrase worth carrying into any funding boom, including the present one. Incred's founder put in serious money of his own.He also tried to rescue an unloved word. Growth, he told the future founders, needs both innovation and bureaucracy, by which he meant not sloth but procedure: the discipline of running something at scale once the experiment has worked. And what, he asked, is the true price of building a global business? Not money, not great products, not fine management. Jet lag.There is an objection to all this, and the talk's opening story supplies it. Twelve winners are twelve survivors. There was no chart for the many lenders of 2017 that, by his own account, did not do well, and no slide for the distressed mill that stayed distressed. The hardest claim came last. Describing Adani Green's vast renewable park at Khavda in Gujarat, on land the state allotted to six developers, Dalmia argued that outsiders overrate government relations and that the real value lies in getting the project built. Adani's speed is on the record: ground broken in 2023, 4.1 gigawatts by the end of 2025. But a sceptic might say that one does not rule out the other. The transcript stops where the questions begin, so I cannot say whether anyone in the room took that up.To his credit, he marks the edges of his own certainty. He flags that his view of Infosys comes from before any disruption by AI. He reads Berkshire's cash pile of some $350 billion as a warning about frothy markets, then adds that time will tell. Having praised Buffett at length, he tells students to read George Soros, who holds nearly the opposite view of markets, as a balance. People selling a system rarely recommend its rival.His last word to the students was junoon. Passion, he said, is what he has seen matter more than anything else, time after time. It is a fine thing to tell twenty-year-olds, and I expect it is true. But he had also told them about Sikar, and he left the two stories side by side without trying to reconcile them. I am not sure they can be reconciled. Every line on his charts starts after somebody has already been chosen. No log scale can show the morning in 1894 when a merchant looked over two neighbouring families and picked one. Or the watchman, more than a century later, still on duty.
Article Summary: Investor Gaurav Dalmia gave students 12 stories about how wealth gets made. The one that stays with you is about how easily it could have gone to someone else. Dalmia chairs Dalmia Group Holdings, which invests in private equity, property and public markets.

Article Title: CBI books Future Retail Ltd, key promoters in Rs 904-crore bank fraud case
Article Text:
CBI conducted coordinated search operations across multiple premises linked to the promoters and directors of the firm in Mumbai.
