NEW DELHI: CBI has registered a major bank fraud case involving Rs 904 crore against Mumbai-based firm Future Retail Ltd. (FRL) and its top leadership, including key promoters Kishore Biyani and Rakesh Biyani on charges of alleged diversion and siphoning of funds.Following registration of the case, the agency conducted coordinated search operations across multiple premises linked to the promoters and directors of the firm in Mumbai. During these raids, investigating officers recovered and seized key incriminating documents relevant to the financial transactions.The case, registered on November 4, also names unknown public servants and other unidentified individuals under charges of criminal conspiracy, cheating, and violations under the Prevention of Corruption Act.The investigative agency launched the probe following a formal complaint lodged by the State Bank of India (SBI), Stressed Assets Management Branch-III, Mumbai. According to the CBI, the retail entity and its executives entered into a criminal conspiracy to obtain extensive credit facilities — including working capital loans, term loans, and letters of credit — from SBI’s Commercial Branch in Fort, Mumbai, as well as a consortium of nine participating banks.Future Retail Ltd previously operated multiple well-known retail formats, including hypermarket and supermarket chains such as Big Bazaar, Fashion@Big Bazaar, and Foodhall, alongside general trading operations in fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG) and fashion products.The CBI's initial findings reveal that the company defrauded the lending institution by willfully failing to utilize the sanctioned bank funds for their intended commercial purposes. Instead, the funds were allegedly siphoned off and illegally diverted through a network of associate companies and connected entities, resulting in a wrongful loss of ₹904.3 crore to the complainant bank and its consortium partners.The CBI stated that ongoing investigations aim to uncover the complete extent of the conspiracy, establish the specific roles of all involved parties — including private individuals and public servants — and trace the ultimate end-use of the diverted loan funds.
Article Summary: CBI has registered a major bank fraud case involving Rs 904 crore against Mumbai-based firm Future Retail Ltd. CBI conducted coordinated search operations across multiple premises linked to the promoters and directors of the firm in Mumbai. During these raids, investigating officers recovered and seized key incriminating documents relevant to the financial transactions.

Article Title: SC ends decades-old power tussle, Himachal to get 11,973 MU from Punjab, Haryana
Article Text:
The BBMB has been providing Himachal Pradesh with its 7.19 per cent share of electricity from these projects since November 1, 2011. However, Punjab and Haryana had not cleared the outstanding dues for the earlier period, amounting to 13,066 MU.

What was the 2011 Supreme Court verdict?

How did the dispute reach the Supreme Court?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Monday settled a decades-old inter-state dispute over unpaid electricity dues from Bhakra Beas Management Board (BBMB) projects, directing Punjab and Haryana to provide Himachal Pradesh with 11,973 million units (MU) of electricity over 20 years. A bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, along with Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, accepted the Centre's proposal to clear the outstanding dues through an energy-based settlement instead of a cash payment.The settlement follows a 2011 Supreme Court verdict that recognised Himachal Pradesh's entitlement to a 7.19 per cent share in the electricity generated by the Bhakra Nangal and Beas hydroelectric projects. The dues date back to 1966, but Punjab and Haryana had not cleared the state's outstanding share for the period before November 2011.Under the arrangement approved by the top court, Punjab and Haryana will provide the electricity over 20 years. The settlement also factors in an adjustment of around Rs 420 crore towards Himachal Pradesh's share of the historical capital costs incurred in building the dams. As a result, the hill state will not have to make any separate payment to Punjab or Haryana.The Centre had earlier proposed that the 13,066 MU in outstanding electricity dues be paid over 15 years, at the rate of 871 MU annually during the lean seasons between October and March. However, the states could not agree on the proposed timeline.Punjab initially opposed the 15-year arrangement and later sought to extend the payment period to 30 years. Himachal Pradesh, on the other hand, wanted the dues cleared within 10 years. The Supreme Court's decision to settle the matter over 20 years brings an end to the prolonged disagreement over the payment schedule.The original electricity arrears were calculated at 13,066 MU by the Central Electricity Authority (CEA). The Centre's proposal had also factored in Himachal Pradesh's liability towards the capital costs of the Bhakra Nangal and Beas projects.According to a report by PTI, the proposal says that Himachal Pradesh's liability was assessed at Rs 420.7 crore, comprising Rs 249.2 crore payable to Punjab and Rs 171.5 crore to Haryana. This represented the state's 7.19 per cent share of the composite of Punjab's outstanding loan-servicing costs for the projects since 1966-67.The Centre had suggested setting off this liability against a portion of the electricity arrears. At the proposed rate of Rs 3.85 per unit, around 1,093 MU would have been adjusted against the capital cost liability.The proposal also provided for the distribution of electricity arrears between Punjab and Haryana in the inter-state ratio of 58:42 for the Bhakra Nangal project and 60:40 for the Beas projects. However, since the states could not reach a consensus on the applicable electricity rate, the Centre recommended settling the dues in energy terms.The Supreme Court's 2011 decision fixed Himachal Pradesh's share in the BBMB projects at 7.19 per cent. Punjab's share was set at 51.80 per cent, while Haryana was allocated 37.51 per cent. Rajasthan's share largely remained unchanged, and Chandigarh's share was fixed at 3.50 per cent.The verdict also specified when Himachal Pradesh's entitlement would take effect for the three projects. The state was entitled to a share in the Bhakra project from November 1, 1966, the Dehar project from November 1977 and the Pong Dam project from January 1978.The BBMB has been providing Himachal Pradesh with its 7.19 per cent share of electricity from these projects since November 1, 2011, PTI reported, citing sources. However, Punjab and Haryana had not cleared the outstanding dues for the earlier period, amounting to 13,066 MU.The dispute dates back to the reorganisation of Punjab under the Punjab Reorganisation Act, 1966. Himachal Pradesh maintained that, as a successor state, it was entitled to a 7.19 per cent share in the BBMB projects and their electricity generation.After efforts to resolve the disagreement between the neighbouring states failed, Himachal Pradesh approached the Supreme Court in 1996 through an original suit. It sought recognition of its entitlement to a share in the projects and the payment of the corresponding arrears.The Centre subsequently attempted to settle the matter outside court. However, with no agreement emerging between the states, the Supreme Court passed a decree on September 27, 2011, upholding Himachal Pradesh's 7.19 per cent entitlement.The latest order accepting the Centre's energy-based settlement provides a mechanism to clear the accumulated dues and closes a dispute that has remained unresolved for decades.
Article Summary: The Supreme Court on Monday settled a decades-old dispute over unpaid electricity dues from Bhakra Beas Management Board projects. Punjab and Haryana will provide Himachal Pradesh with 11,973 million units (MU) of electricity over 20 years. The dispute dates back to the reorganisation of Punjab under the Punjab Reorganisation Act, 1966.

Article Title: OBC creamy layer row: SC protects past jobs, promotions but leaves pending cases open
Article Text:
The government has maintained that it is not challenging or seeking a review of the March 11 judgment.

Centre flags concerns over past recruitments

Dispute over salary-based creamy layer criteria

Centre seeks time to frame uniform mechanism

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Friday clarified that its March 11 ruling on determining the creamy layer status of Other Backward Class (OBC) candidates would not reopen completed appointments, promotions or seniority positions.The top court said cases that are still pending would be examined individually by the courts, based on their merits and the candidates' eligibility.A bench of Justice Pamidighantam Sri Narasimha and Justice R Mahadevan delivered the ruling while hearing an application filed by the Centre seeking clarity on how the March 11 judgment should be implemented. The Court also extended the deadline for compliance with its earlier directions by eight weeks.The clarification comes after the Centre raised concerns that applying the March 11 ruling retrospectively could unsettle years of government recruitments, service allocations and admissions to educational institutions.In its application, the government argued that applying the revised interpretation to past cases could affect appointments and admissions made under the rules and eligibility criteria in force at the time.It warned that this could create uncertainty over OBC-NCL status, seniority, service conditions and career progression.“Retrospective or belated application of a changed eligibility criterion may unsettle appointments and admissions made under the rules and certificates prevailing at the relevant time and may create uncertainty regarding OBC-NCL status, seniority, service conditions and career progression. It may also affect admissions to Central and State educational institutions, universities and professional institutions. The Applicant therefore respectfully submits that the temporal operation of the Judgment requires clarification so as to avoid unsettling completed selections, appointments and admissions and the consequential rights arising therefrom”, the plea stated as per LiveLaw.The Centre said more than 5.69 lakh reserved vacancies, including 3.70 lakh OBC vacancies, were filled in Central government ministries, departments and their subordinate offices between 2016 and 2025.These recruitments were conducted under the August 8, 1993 Office Memorandum and subsequent government instructions.It argued that retrospective implementation could also necessitate a review of service allocations made through Civil Services Examinations since 2012. This could potentially lead to changes in the services and cadres allotted to officers already in government service, affecting their seniority and promotion prospects.The government also flagged possible complications in recruitment examinations conducted by the Railways, banks, Department of Posts and paramilitary organisations. It said similar disputes could arise in 18 States and Union Territories that follow the 1993 guidelines.The Centre further pointed out that candidates who become eligible for technical services several years after an examination might no longer meet the prescribed physical and medical standards. It also warned that reopening admissions granted to lakhs of students in universities and professional institutions could create difficulties, particularly where there are no provisions for additional seats.The clarification application stems from the Supreme Court's March 11 judgment on how the creamy layer among OBC candidates should be identified.The Court had ruled that a parent's salary alone cannot be used to determine whether an OBC candidate belongs to the creamy layer. The nature and category of the post held by the parents must also be taken into account.The dispute centred on two government instructions, the Office Memorandum issued on August 8, 1993, and a subsequent clarification dated October 14, 2004.The 1993 memorandum laid down the criteria for identifying the OBC creamy layer. It did not make a parent's salary the sole basis for exclusion from reservation benefits. Under the applicable Income/Wealth Test, salary and agricultural income are excluded from the income calculation, while the status and category of the parent's post remain relevant under the prescribed criteria.The 2004 clarification dealt with employees working in organisations such as public sector undertakings (PSUs), banks, universities and private companies, where the equivalence of their posts with government positions had not been established. It provided for consideration of parents' salary income in such cases.The Supreme Court held that the 2004 clarification could not introduce a new condition that was not part of the original 1993 policy. It also observed that treating children of PSU and private-sector employees differently from those of similarly placed government employees could amount to hostile discrimination and violate Articles 14 and 16 of the Constitution, which guarantee equality before the law and equal opportunity in public employment.The government has maintained that it is not challenging or seeking a review of the March 11 judgment. Instead, it wants clarity on when the ruling should apply and how its directions should be implemented.The Centre has sought two years to consult stakeholders, establish equivalence between posts in non-government organisations and government positions, and develop a uniform mechanism for determining creamy-layer status in cases where such equivalence has not been established.It has also asked the SC not to disturb completed selections, appointments, service and cadre allocations, seniority positions and admissions made under the eligibility rules applicable at the time. The government has separately sought clarity on candidates who were already participating in examinations or recruitment processes when the March 11 judgment was delivered.In a separate interim application, the Centre sought permission to proceed with service allocation for 958 candidates recommended by the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) in the Civil Services Examination 2025, using the existing 1993 framework while the clarification application remained pending.The government argued that any further delay would push back the candidates' Foundation Course, training and induction schedules. It said the resulting disruption could not be reversed even if the Court eventually accepted its position.
Article Summary: The top court said cases that are still pending would be examined individually by the courts, based on their merits and the candidates' eligibility. The Court also extended the deadline for compliance with its earlier directions by eight weeks. The Centre raised concerns that applying the March 11 ruling retrospectively could unsettle years of government recruitments.

Article Title: Watch: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay launches one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns
Article Text:
Vijay presented 22-carat, one-gram gold rings to 25 newborns. (PTI)

Who is eligible for the gold ring?

Scheme draws on Tamil tradition

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. He also held some of the newborns and presented the rings to beneficiaries during the launch programme.Under the scheme, eligible babies born in government hospitals and government primary health centres will receive a 22-carat, one-gram gold ring.The initiative, named the Maternal Uncle Gold Ring Scheme (Thaaimaman Thanga Mothiram Thittam), has an annual allocation of Rs 755.83 crore.It is aimed at celebrating motherhood, promoting maternal and child health and encouraging institutional deliveries by increasing public confidence in government healthcare facilities.The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions.Mothers must be registered under the Pregnancy and Infant Cohort Monitoring and Evaluation (PICME) system and have a Reproductive and Child Health (RCH) ID. They will also have to provide an e-KYC-verified Aadhaar card along with one of the prescribed identity or residence documents.These include ration cards, voter identity cards, Labour Welfare Board identity cards, Department of Posts address cards and nativity certificates.The state government has already procured 1.28 lakh one-gram gold rings for the initial rollout. Each ring will have a unique serial number and will be packed in tamper-proof packaging.From Monday, babies born in government hospitals will receive the rings at the time of discharge, according to the state government.To clear the backlog of eligible babies born between June 22 and Monday, the government will distribute the rings through 107 hubs across Tamil Nadu.Distribution will begin at the rate of 100 babies per day at each hub. At designated centres, 25 beneficiaries will be accommodated in the morning and another 25 in the afternoon to avoid overcrowding, PTI reported.Village Health Nurses will distribute invitations informing beneficiaries of their allotted date and time. Beneficiaries have been asked to visit the designated centres only at the time mentioned in their invitations.The district administration has also made transportation arrangements for beneficiaries from their respective areas. Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election as a symbolic gift to newborns, drawing on the Tamil tradition of ‘Thaimaaman Seer’. The scheme has retrospective effect from June 22, Vijay’s birthday.A government order issued on June 23 described the initiative as a token celebrating the birth of a child, motherhood and the cultural tradition of ‘Thaimaaman’.According to ANI, Tamil Nadu minister Arun Raj explained the cultural significance of the initiative saying, "A maternal uncle is someone who is among the first to rush in when a child is born, sharing in his sister’s happiness as his own. He assures her that he will always stand by her and her child, offering love, support and a sense of security.""Today, the Tamil Nadu Government, under the leadership of our brother, Mr. Vijay, is embracing this sacred bond of the maternal uncle and, as a gesture of that affection, is set to provide a one-gram gold ring to every child born in government hospitals. When the scheme was announced and the question arose as to where it should be launched, the place chosen by our Chief Minister was Madurai. This is the sacred soil of Madurai, blessed with the compassion and grace of Mother Meenakshi," he added.Tamil Nadu records around 7.8 lakh deliveries annually, with institutional deliveries accounting for 99.9% of births, according to NFHS-6. Government health facilities account for nearly 4.2 lakh deliveries, or around 53% of the total.According to the state government, the average out-of-pocket expenditure for a delivery at a government hospital is Rs 1,364, compared with Rs 63,473 at a private hospital.The government said the scheme is intended to encourage safe institutional deliveries, strengthen maternal and child welfare and increase public trust in government healthcare services.The Tamil Nadu Medical Services Corporation will procure the gold rings based on annual requirements, while a project and programme management unit will oversee implementation and monitoring.
Article Summary: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions. Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election.

Article Title: Delhi landfill garbage mountains shrinking, 100 acres reclaimed in 18 months: CM Rekha Gupta
Article Text:
Delhi CM Rekha Gupta poses for a group picture during an on-site inspection of waste disposal operations near Okhla, in New Delhi

Government targets legacy and fresh waste

New processing plants at three sites

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Poll Vote & Share your view What is your top concern regarding pollution in Delhi? Landfill waste Air quality Water quality (Yamuna) Dust pollution 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Focus on pollution and waste management

NEW DELHI: Delhi chief minister Rekha Gupta on Saturday said the garbage mountains at the city's landfill sites were steadily shrinking as she reviewed waste disposal work at Okhla and laid the foundation stone for new waste processing facilities at Okhla, Ghazipur and Singhola.Gupta said the Delhi government had reclaimed 100 acres of land across the city's three landfill sites over the past one-and-a-half years, with a large portion of the cleared area also being turned green.She said almost all legacy waste at Okhla that existed before January 2025 had been processed."Today, at Okhla, we have processed almost all the legacy waste that was there before January 2025," Gupta said.Gupta said the government was working on two fronts: clearing the existing garbage mountains while ensuring that fresh waste generated every day did not accumulate into new landfill sites.According to news agency ANI, she said around 3,000-4,000 metric tonnes of fresh waste reaches the sites daily and is being processed round the clock."The garbage currently piled up here is essentially fresh waste generated after January 2025, and that too is being processed round the clock. So, we are fighting on two fronts: one is eliminating waste, and the other is ensuring that the 3,000 to 4,000 metric tons of fresh waste arriving daily is processed immediately, so that new garbage mountains are not formed for future generations," Gupta said.She said the government was working to reduce the existing garbage mountains to zero."People are seeing that the garbage mountains are continuously shrinking and soon a time will come when they will become zero," Gupta said.Gupta also said she had taken what she described as her "last selfie" with the garbage mountain at Okhla."Today I have taken my last selfie with the garbage mountain; after this I have taken a pledge that this garbage mountain will end soon," she said.Taking a jibe at the Opposition, Gupta added, "I had said - garbage mountain, you will have to go; the opposition mocked. Today I will say the garbage mountain is going; now only its back remains."During the programme at the Okhla SLF site, Gupta laid the foundation stone for fresh waste processing plants at Okhla, Ghazipur and Singhola, as well as a biogas facility at Ghazipur. She also inaugurated the M&CW Centre at Kotla Mubarakpur through virtual mode from Okhla.The Okhla plant will be built at a cost of Rs 103 crore and will have a processing capacity of 1,400 metric tonnes per day.The Singhola facility will cost Rs 42 crore and have a capacity of 800 metric tonnes per day, while the Ghazipur plant will have a processing capacity of 700 metric tonnes per day.The facilities are intended to process fresh waste as well as construction and demolition waste. Gupta said the new units would also produce biogas, green energy and manure."Waste should not remain waste; Delhi should use it as wealth," she said, adding that new technologies were being introduced for waste segregation and processing.She said waste and cattle dung would be used to produce biogas and manure as part of efforts to build a technology-driven waste management system.Gupta said the government was taking up several measures to address pollution, including work on landfill waste, cleaning the Yamuna, dust mitigation, plantation, road infrastructure and waste management."Our government is tackling pollution from a 360-degree perspective to ensure it gradually decreases. We are working on every aspect, be it addressing the mountains of garbage, cleaning the Yamuna, improving road infrastructure, or managing waste, to ensure the people of Delhi enjoy better air quality. Our resolve and policies are absolutely clear, and we are working 24x7 in the public interest," she said.The chief minister also reviewed the progress of waste disposal work with officials and directed them to accelerate the work according to the stipulated timeline.She said the garbage mountains at Bhalswa, Ghazipur and Okhla had caused inconvenience to people travelling through these areas and said the government was continuing efforts to eliminate them.
Article Summary: Gupta said the Delhi government had reclaimed 100 acres of land across the city's three landfill sites over the past one-and-a-half years. She said almost all legacy waste at Okhla that existed before January 2025 had been processed. Gupta said the new units would also produce biogas, green energy and manure.

Article Title: India-US trade talks hit ‘plateau’: Sitharaman says further give-and-take ‘very, very difficult’
Article Text:
Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman

India stresses strategic autonomy in trade negotiations

India-EU pact opens market access

India and US have reached a “plateau” in negotiations over their bilateral trade agreement, with further concessions from either side likely to be "very very difficult", finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman said on Monday. Speaking at the Munich Leaders Meeting in New Delhi, she said that while negotiations are still underway, any progress from here would depend on whether there was limited room for compromise on either side.“The agreement negotiations are still ongoing, although we'd like to believe that both the sides have reached a plateau beyond which giving or taking might be very, very difficult. But maybe if there are rooms to operate from, both sides would do it,” Sitharaman said.She said the agreement was still being “hard and very rigorously negotiated” and that India has a trade surplus with the US. “But what is the predominant feature of the trade relations between India and the US? The trade balance is very much in our favor.”Sitharaman said that the US would naturally want to reduce this trade imbalance and address what it sees as losses built up over the years.She also said that the way countries negotiate trade deals was changing, with governments now looking beyond traditional negotiations to address trade imbalances.“Negotiation used to be the only platform through which countries could highlight the discrepancies, highlight the lop-sidedness and say, would we want to correct this?” she said.“Tariff was an instrument of negotiation, and tariff had a certain framework within which you will apply it. Today framework is there, tariffs are going,” she said, while stressing that countries still need to negotiate and find “some give and take”.Sitharaman was also asked about maintaining strategic autonomy while negotiating bilateral trade agreements with European countries, including in the context of India procuring Russian oil."There is no Lindsay Graham Bill in Europe...," she said.On the broader question of how bilateral trade agreements can protect a country's interests in an era of multilateralism, Sitharaman said countries were increasingly choosing bilateral partnerships where they saw greater benefit.“Countries choose where multilateralism would benefit them, and there are some unique bilaterals which countries choose to have. The balance is somewhat tilted in favour of the bilateral rather than the multilateral,” she said.She said countries were now increasingly looking for new trade partners and strengthening those relationships through agreements.“Countries are now rapidly catching up with — I would put the EU-India also in a bilateral mode -because it's one in the name of union, but of course within them they have. So, bilaterals today are catching up far more than even initiating or beginning a multilateral. It's not deliberate, but in a way, if you don't do it, you're not moving forward. Countries will have to choose new partners for their trade and strengthen the tie through an agreement. And therefore, newer partnerships are being searched for, and they are tied up bilaterally.”FM Sitharaman cited the India-EU trade agreement as a major example of India's approach to negotiating trade pacts while protecting domestic interests.She said India had opened 92.5 per cent of its tariff lines and around 97 per cent of tariff value under the agreement. The EU, meanwhile, had opened 99 per cent in value terms and possibly 97 per cent of tariff lines.According to Sitharaman, greater access to the European market could support employment in labour-intensive sectors, including footwear, textiles, toys and processed products. Many of these sectors are linked to micro and small enterprises.“Those are all in the micro and small medium industry segment, which are labor-intensive,” Sitharaman said, adding that greater access to the European market could generate “more exports, more jobs”.Sitharaman said bilateral trade agreements were becoming increasingly important as multilateral institutions have weakened.“Multilateralism is not going to go away. But multilateralism has weakened,” she said.She also stressed that multilateralism should continue even as countries increasingly pursue bilateral agreements.“Multilateralism is not going to go away and multilateralism shouldn't go away,” Sitharaman said.The Munich Leaders Meeting, being held in the National Capital, provides a platform for about 100 senior decision-makers and experts to discuss opportunities for stronger cooperation among emerging and middle powers amid profound geopolitical change. Discussions include geoeconomic developments, trade and connectivity, maritime security, defence cooperation and other key international challenges.
Article Summary: Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman says India and US have reached a 'plateau' in negotiations over their bilateral trade agreement. She said any progress from here would depend on whether there was limited room for compromise on either side. She also said the way countries negotiate trade deals was changing, with governments now looking beyond traditional negotiations to address trade imbalances.

Article Title: Jio IPO sees bumper demand: India's largest public issue fully subscribed in just 100 minutes of opening
Article Text:
The IPO is open to retail investors, employees and eligible Reliance shareholders.

Jio IPO

Jio IPO: Jio Platforms' $3.2 billion initial public offering (IPO) was fully subscribed within less than two hours of bidding opening on Wednesday, as investors rushed to participate in India's biggest-ever share sale. The offering is also the first IPO from billionaire Mukesh Ambani 's Reliance group in two decades.According to a PTI report, the Jio IPO was fully subscribed within 100 minutes of its opening on October 21.The rapid subscription was notable because large IPOs in India often see a slow start, with institutional investors typically placing their bids closer to the closing deadline. By comparison, the National Stock Exchange of India's share sale recently attracted subscriptions for just 42% of the shares on offer on its first day. Hyundai Motor India's IPO had received bids for only 18% of its offering on the opening day.Also Read | Jio IPO, India’s largest public issue, opens for subscription: Price band, GMP to brokerage views - top 10 things to know The IPO is open to retail investors, employees and eligible Reliance shareholders. The issue will close on Friday, with shares priced in a band of Rs 1,065 to Rs 1,119 apiece.Exchange data showed that institutional investors had bid for 3.25 times the shares reserved for them by Wednesday. Retail participation was lower at that stage, with individual investors applying for 0.22 times their reserved quota.Retail investors have been allocated around one-third of the total offering.The IPO values Jio Platforms at as much as $108.3 billion. Once trading begins on October 28, the company could rank among India's largest listed companies by market capitalisation.Earlier this week, Jio Platforms allotted shares worth $853 million to domestic and international investors, including the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority and BlackRock. The anchor investor portion attracted bids exceeding $25 billion, according to a Reuters report.Backed by global investors such as Meta, Google's parent company Alphabet and other institutional investors, Jio Platforms houses India's largest telecom operator. With more than 500 million subscribers, the business is the world's second-largest telecom operator within a single country, behind China Mobile.This is Reliance's first IPO since 2006. Jio Platforms' telecom business, led by Ambani's son Akash, began operations in 2016. Its strategy was built around the expectation that Indians would use the internet much more extensively if access became almost free. By offering inexpensive data and free voice calls, Jio quickly gained market share from competitors such as Bharti Airtel and Vodafone Idea.
Article Summary: Jio IPO was fully subscribed within 100 minutes of its opening on October 21. The rapid subscription was notable because large IPOs in India often see a slow start. The IPO is open to retail investors, employees and eligible Reliance shareholders. The issue will close on Friday, with shares priced in a band of Rs 1,065 to Rs1,119 apiece.

Article Title: LPG consumption down, diesel & petrol sales up in September
Article Text:
LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier

NEW DELHI: LPG demand fell by over 9% year-on-year in Sept, while petrol and diesel sales registered growth of 7% and 5%, respectively, provisional data released by the Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell (PPAC) showed.LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier.Month-on-month consumption, however, registered a growth of 8%, up from 2.4 MT.Petrol sales increased from 3.4 MT in Sept last year to 3.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose from 6.8 MT to 7.1 MT. Petrol and diesel consumption had registered year-on-year growth of 7.9% and 6.5%, respectively, in July.While petrol is largely used as an automobile fuel and its consumption is commensurate with the increasing number of vehicles, diesel is consumed by transport vehicles for passenger and freight movement, besides being used in the agricultural sector.Erratic monsoon conditions due to El Nino boosted demand for diesel for irrigation.Cumulative petrol consumption during Apr-Sept in the current financial year increased 7% to 22.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose 4.8% to 47.9 MT. In contrast, LPG consumption declined 14.9% to 13.8 MT from 16.2 MT during the corresponding period of 2025-26.
Article Summary: LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier. Petrol sales increased from 3.4 MT in Sept last year to 3.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose from 6.8 MT to 7.1 MT.

Article Title: In 2024, Eva Longoria received $50 million from Jeff Bezos and Lauren Sanchez for philanthropy; two years later, she says you don't have to be a billionaire to make a difference
Article Text:
Eva Longoria received $50 million from Jeff Bezos and Lauren Sánchez in 2024 through the Bezos Courage and Civility Award. (Photo: Instagram)

What Eva Longoria did with Jeff Bezos' $50 million award

Two years after receiving the award, Longoria says philanthropy is not just about how much money a person has, but how they contribute to society. (Photo: Getty)

Eva Longoria is mentoring small-business owners

Eva Longoria believes mentoring, supporting small businesses and sharing knowledge are meaningful ways to make a difference, even without being wealthy. (Photo: Eva Longoria Foundation)

From Van Jones to Eva Longoria: The Bezos Courage and Civility Award

In March 2024, actor and entrepreneur Eva Longoria received $50 million from Amazon founder Jeff Bezos and his wife, Lauren Sanchez Bezos, through their Courage and Civility Award. Two years later, the Desperate Housewives star has a message about philanthropy: you don't have to be rich or famous to make a difference.In an interview with Fortune, Longoria spoke about one of the biggest misconceptions surrounding charitable work, saying that people often associate meaningful impact with the amount of money someone can donate. She believes, however, that even small acts of support can help bring about change.“One of the biggest misconceptions about philanthropy is that impact is tied to wealth or scale, when in reality, impact comes in many forms,” Longoria told the publication. “What I’ve learned is that impact doesn’t come from how much money you have, it comes from how you show up.”Her message comes at a time when large donations from billionaires often dominate conversations about philanthropy. Longoria believes that giving back should not be seen as something only wealthy individuals can afford to do. According to her, mentoring someone, supporting a small business or sharing professional knowledge can also make a meaningful difference.“Mentoring someone, supporting small business, sharing what you know—those things matter because not everyone has access to capital or resources, but anyone can be part of someone else’s support system,” she added. “And I think that’s really what’s missing for a lot of people. They don’t have someone in their corner.”Longoria and retired US Navy Admiral Bill McRaven received $50 million each in March 2024. The grants were part of the Bezos Courage and Civility Award, launched by Bezos and Sanchez in 2021 to recognise individuals making significant contributions to society. The award allows recipients to direct the funds towards charitable causes of their choice.For Longoria, the recognition was about more than the financial contribution. She said the award represented trust and responsibility and encouraged her to become more intentional and strategic in her advocacy.“Receiving that support was incredibly meaningful, not just because of the scale of the gift, but because it represented trust and responsibility,” she said.The actress explained that the grant had allowed her to continue investing in communities and causes close to her heart, particularly supporting Latina entrepreneurs, expanding access to education and backing organisations working towards change on the ground.“This award has allowed me to continue investing those resources into the communities and causes I care deeply about—supporting Latina entrepreneurs, expanding access to education, and backing organizations that are driving real change on the ground,” she said.Longoria added that the award had helped the Eva Longoria Foundation create long-term impact through transformative giving. Founded in 2012, the foundation works to improve educational and entrepreneurial opportunities for Latinas in the United States.She is also associated with Eva's Heroes, a charity that supports young adults with intellectual special needs.Apart from her foundation work, Longoria is also putting her belief in community-level support into practice through a new partnership with Lenovo, under which she is mentoring small-business owners.The actor has built a business portfolio that includes luxury tequila brand Casa Del Sol, media company Hyphenate Media Group and a stake in women's soccer team Angel City FC. She has also made an early investment in the John Wick franchise.Despite her business success and the resources available to her, Longoria believes that people do not need substantial financial means to help someone else succeed. She sees guidance, mentorship and access to opportunities as important forms of giving.Bezos and Lauren Sanchez Bezos launched the Courage and Civility Award in 2021 for individuals who make significant contributions to society. Previous recipients include CNN commentator and civil rights advocate Van Jones, chef and humanitarian Jose Andres, and country music legend Dolly Parton.Jones and Andres were among the first recipients, each receiving $100 million. Parton received $100 million in 2022, with her philanthropic work including support for research that helped fund Moderna's COVID-19 vaccine development.In 2024, Eva Longoria and McRaven each received $50 million. McRaven, who oversaw the 2011 US military raid that killed al-Qaeda leader Osama bin Laden, pledged to use his share for educational programmes for future military leaders and children of deceased veterans, as well as mental health support for military personnel.The Giving Pledge, co-founded by Bill Gates, Melinda French Gates and Warren Buffett in 2010, is another initiative encouraging large-scale philanthropy. It asks billionaires to commit at least half of their wealth to charitable causes. However, questions have been raised about how quickly such pledges translate into actual donations.Two years after receiving the $50 million award, Longoria's message is that philanthropy is not measured only by the size of a cheque. While the grant has given her the resources to support causes on a larger scale, she believes anyone can make a difference by offering their time, knowledge and support to someone who needs it.
Article Summary: Eva Longoria received $50 million from Jeff Bezos and Lauren Sánchez in 2024. Two years later, the Desperate Housewives star has a message about philanthropy. Longoria believes you don't have to be rich or famous to make a difference. She believes mentoring, supporting small businesses and sharing knowledge are meaningful ways to help.

Article Title: A New York buyer offered $550,000 cash for a Bronx home damaged by a fallen tree, then demanded a $270,000 price cut and sued for $1 million; a November 5 appeals court has upheld dismissal of his law
Article Text:
Representative image

A home sold with warnings

What the contract said

The demand for $270,000

The $1 million lawsuit

Why the buyer’s claim failed

Representative image

The limits of an as-is clause

A cautionary real estate lesson

A New York buyer who offered $550,000 in cash for a severely damaged Bronx home later demanded a $270,000 price reduction and sued for $1 million when the seller refused. On November 5, 2026, the Appellate Division, First Department upheld the dismissal of Vedat Rexhepi’s lawsuit against Astoria Park Realty LLC, ruling that the buyer had knowingly agreed to purchase the unsafe property in an as-is transaction and could not use a later damage claim to escape the deal, as per a report on Justia U.S. Law.The dispute began with a property that had already been badly damaged by a fallen tree in March 2018. The New York City Department of Buildings issued an unsafe building violation, and the eventual sale listing disclosed unsafe conditions caused by water damage from the fallen tree. The buyer’s claim that he was entitled to a major discount was rejected because the contract, disclosures and photographs showed he understood exactly what he was buying. Read more about it here:When the Bronx property was listed for sale, the listing did not hide its condition. It expressly disclosed unsafe conditions due to water damage from a fallen tree, stated that the property would be sold as is, prohibited interior access, and required cash-only offers supported by proof of funds.In February 2024, Vedat Rexhepi offered $550,000 for the property. His written letter of intent acknowledged that the offer was as is, without inspection and for cash.The memorandum of sale also stated that no inspection would take place because the home was deemed unsafe.The seller’s broker provided interior photographs showing extensive damage and unsafe conditions. The buyer then signed a purchase contract that same month, after being given a clear picture of the property’s condition before committing to the deal.The contract contained an important provision about who bore the risk if the property’s condition changed before closing. Its preamble included a standard disclaimer stating that, absent a contrary contractual provision, General Obligations Law section 5-1311 would govern casualty loss occurring before closing.Paragraph 12 went further. It expressly acknowledged that the buyer was aware of the property’s physical condition and required him to accept it as is, subject only to reasonable use, wear, tear and natural deterioration between contract and closing. It also stated that there would be no reduction in the purchase price or claim of any kind for any change in the property’s condition.The buyer paid a $55,000 down payment, which was held in escrow by the seller’s attorney. By agreement, that money was later applied toward water charges discovered during the title search.By October 2024, the seller was trying to schedule the closing, but the buyer’s lawyer said he needed more time to secure funds. The seller set a time-of-the-essence closing for December 3, 2024, and the parties twice agreed to postpone it, ultimately rescheduling for January 28, 2025.Five days before the closing, the buyer, now represented by new counsel, demanded a $270,000 reduction in the purchase price. He relied on General Obligations Law section 5-1311, claiming that he had seen new damage through a window during the preceding week and that the damage exceeded normal wear, tear and natural deterioration.He estimated repairs at $270,000, but the court noted that the claim was unsupported by an engineering report, contractor estimate or other documentation. The seller rejected the demand, saying the conditions described were the same unsafe and deteriorated conditions disclosed before the contract was signed. The buyer then failed to appear at the January 28 closing and did not tender the remaining balance.After the failed closing, the buyer sued for breach of contract. He sought specific performance with a $270,000 purchase-price reduction, or alternatively $1 million in damages. He also filed a notice of pendency against the property, a legal step often used in real estate disputes to put third parties on notice of a claimed interest.The seller moved to dismiss the complaint based on the contract, property listings, precontract photographs, correspondence and evidence of the failed closing. The seller also submitted affidavits from its managing member and broker stating that the alleged damage predated the contract.The Bronx trial court dismissed the case. On Nov. 5, 2026, the First Department unanimously affirmed that dismissal.The appellate court said the buyer had expressly waived inspection before signing the contract. That meant his allegations about the property’s precontract interior condition were speculative and not based on firsthand knowledge, and the court was not required to accept them.The documentary evidence was also decisive. The listings, precontract photographs, correspondence and contractual disclosures showed that the buyer was fully aware of the property’s severely damaged and unsafe condition before agreeing to buy it. In the court’s view, those materials contradicted his claim that he had contracted to purchase a materially different property from the one the seller offered to convey.The buyer argued that General Obligations Law section 5-1311 entitled him to a reduction. That law allocates the risk of pre-closing loss, but only when the contract does not expressly allocate that risk. Here, paragraph 12 did exactly that, stating that the buyer would accept the property as is, subject to natural deterioration, without a price reduction or claim for any change in condition.The court was careful to note that an as-is clause does not automatically bar every claim under section 5-1311. But the facts mattered. The buyer knowingly accepted the risks of purchasing a severely damaged, unsafe property that he was not entitled to inspect.Even if the buyer was correct that the property suffered additional damage after the contract was signed, the court said his allegations did not show that the damage was a material casualty loss separate from the natural deterioration expected from the hazardous and unsafe conditions disclosed before the sale.In other words, the buyer could not invoke the statute as a way to obtain a substantial discount for risks he had already agreed to assume. The appellate court therefore upheld dismissal of the lawsuit and awarded costs to the seller.The case shows why buyers should read every clause in a distressed-property contract, especially when a home is being sold as is and without interior access. A cash offer may speed up a transaction, but it does not remove the legal consequences of accepting a property in poor condition.It also demonstrates the value of documentation. The seller’s listings, photographs, disclosures and contract language gave the court a clear record of what the buyer knew before signing. When a buyer later sought a $270,000 reduction and $1 million in damages, that record proved fatal to the claim.What are your views on this? Tell us in the comments below.
Article Summary: A New York buyer who offered $550,000 in cash for a severely damaged Bronx home later demanded a $270,000 price reduction and sued for $1 million when the seller refused. The Appellate Division, First Department upheld the dismissal of Vedat Rexhepi’s lawsuit against Astoria Park Realty LLC, ruling that the buyer had knowingly agreed to purchase the unsafe property in an as-is transaction.

Article Title: Rs 6.86 crore Mumbai flat in Lower Parel sold for Rs 5.36 crore, Rs 5 crore adjusted as brokerage; Lodha Developers alleges Rs 6.67 crore loss in Mankoli land acquisition and Lower Parel flat deal; fi
Article Text:
Image Used For Representational Purpose Only





MUMBAI: Lodha Developers Ltd has lodged a fresh complaint against its former director, business development officer Shivaji Jadhav and others, alleging that they caused a financial loss of Rs 6.67 crore to the company through irregularities in a land acquisition deal at Mankoli in Bhiwandi, Thane district, and a related flat transaction in Lower Parel.This is the third case registered against Rajendra Lodha.The company lodged an FIR with the NM Joshi Marg police, which has since been transferred to the city crime branch. The alleged irregularities involved a purported Rs 5 crore brokerage agreement, a Rs 1.5 crore discount on a luxury apartment and payments made in connection with the acquisition of 6,420 square metres of land.The land in question is located in Mankoli village. The company entered into a development agreement with Chandrasen Bhoir and his family in January 2019. Under the agreement, the landowners were to receive 24,075 square feet of saleable built-up area in exchange for the agricultural land.Subsequently, Avinash Bhoir claimed possession of a portion of the land, following which the company entered into a supplementary agreement to provide him with 1,425 square feet of saleable built-up area. Nitin Keni also claimed possession of land covered by the three survey numbers.According to the complaint, the company entered into a supplementary agreement with Keni on May 4, 2019, and paid him Rs 17 lakh in connection with his claim.The complaint alleges that Haridas Bhoir acted as a broker in the original land transaction and received Rs 8.5 lakh. However, the company subsequently discovered alleged irregularities involving Sackveer Builds and Developers LLP, whose representatives, Sachin K Dhaktode and Virji K Dhadi, had purchased Flat No. B-5802 at Lodha Alura, Lodha Park, Lower Parel.According to the complaint, the flat was originally priced at Rs 6.86 crore. On the recommendation of then director Rajendra Lodha, its price was allegedly reduced by around Rs 1.5 crore, and the property was sold for approximately Rs 5.36 crore. The flat was registered on July 19, 2019.The complaint further alleges that an inter-office note dated July 30, 2019, signed by Rajendra Lodha and Shivaji Jadhav, directed that Rs 5 crore be adjusted against the flat's purchase price, purportedly towards brokerage for the Mankoli land transaction.A brokerage agreement was subsequently executed on July 31, 2019, between Sackveer Builds and Developers LLP and Lodha Developers Pvt Ltd. The agreement, signed on behalf of the company by Babusingh Rajguru, allegedly provided for a payment of ₹5 crore for making the land title clear and marketable. An affidavit submitted by the developers' representatives also referred to the payment.However, an internal investigation allegedly found that Sackveer Builds and Developers LLP had no involvement in the acquisition of the Mankoli land. The company further claimed that neither the brokerage agreement nor the inter-office note could be found in its records during the review of the transactions.The complaint alleges that Rajendra Lodha, Shivaji Jadhav, Babusingh Rajguru and others misused the authority entrusted to them and conspired to route the alleged brokerage amount through the flat transaction. The FIR names six individuals in connection with the alleged Rs 6.67 crore loss, comprising the Rs 5 crore brokerage adjustment, the Rs 1.5 crore discount and the Rs 17 lakh payment to Keni.Interestingly, the original complaint submitted to the police did not name Rajendra Lodha. However, following a preliminary inquiry, the police allegedly found his involvement and included his name in the FIR.
Article Summary: Lodha Developers Ltd has lodged a fresh complaint against its former director, business development officer Shivaji Jadhav and others. The alleged irregularities involved a purported Rs 5 crore brokerage agreement, a Rs 1.5 crore discount on a luxury apartment and payments made in connection with the acquisition of 6,420 square metres of land.

Article Title: Bengaluru-Goa Vande Bharat to impact 13 trains on coastal route
Article Text:
The railway ministry has announced the introduction of Vande Bharat service between Yeshwantpur and Madgaon





BENGALURU: A faster, more comfortable ride on Vande Bharat Express from Bengaluru to Goa is on the cards, but its introduction may lead to rescheduling of 13 existing trains and disrupting passenger-friendly arrival and departure timings.Last Saturday, the railway ministry notified the introduction of Vande Bharat service between Yeshwantpur and Madgaon, assigning numbers 26655 and 26656. The Vande Bharat will operate six days a week from Yeshwantpur, departing at 7.35am, except on Wednesdays.A railway official said to facilitate 1,100 passengers on Vande Bharat, around 15,000 regular travellers will be affected. A senior South Western Railway official said the new service would be accorded priority through the ghat section.The train will traverse the recently electrified ghat section between Sakleshpur and Subrahmanya Road, a 55km stretch where all trains are restricted to a maximum speed of 30kmph because of the challenging terrain and safety concerns.Among the biggest casualties would be train No. 16516 Karwar-Yeshwantpur Express. The train, which currently reaches Bengaluru at 8.50pm, will arrive at 10.15pm under the revised schedule.An even bigger blow awaits passengers travelling on train No. 16576 Mangaluru Junction-Yeshwantpur Gomteshwara Express. A popular option for passengers travelling from Mangaluru to Bengaluru, the train currently reaches Yeshwantpur at 4.30pm. Under the revised schedule, it will leave Mangaluru at 11.40am and reach Bengaluru at 10.15pm.The change also takes away much of the convenience of its existing schedule for passengers planning to reach Bengaluru by late afternoon. The train, which has a vistadome coach offering panoramic views of the Western Ghats, will continue to provide the scenic experience, but at a considerably different time of day.In another notable change, train No. 22679 Yeshwantpur-Hassan Superfast Express will see its average speed fall below 55kmph in both directions. Several other trains operating along the corridor will face en-route regulation of between 10 and 25 minutes.
Article Summary: Vande Bharat will operate six days a week from Yeshwantpur, departing at 7.35am, except on Wednesdays. Around 15,000 regular travellers will be affected by the new service. The train will traverse the recently electrified ghat section.

Article Title: Bursting firecrackers in Delhi this Diwali? Check timings, restrictions and penalties
Article Text:
Residents must adhere to specific time slots for bursting firecrackers (Representative image)





NEW DELHI: Delhi residents will be allowed to burst certified green firecrackers only on November 7 and 8, between 6am and 7am and 8pm and 10pm, as the city prepares for Diwali amid worsening air quality and a thick layer of smog.The Delhi government has appealed to residents to follow the Supreme Court’s directions on the sale and use of green firecrackers across Delhi-NCR.The district magistrate (East), in an order, said bursting firecrackers outside the prescribed hours would be strictly prohibited, news agency PTI reported.Only green firecrackers certified by the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research-National Environmental Engineering Research Institute (CSIR-NEERI) will be permitted for sale.The firecracker boxes must be properly sealed and carry valid product- and batch-specific QR codes, the order said.Sales will be allowed only at locations designated by Delhi Police. Sale from unauthorised locations and online platforms has been prohibited.The administration has also directed joint enforcement teams comprising district officials and Delhi Police personnel to conduct regular inspections and prevent the sale and use of prohibited firecrackers, PTI reported.The order also prohibits bursting firecrackers within a 300-metre radius of hospitals, nursing homes, health centres, old-age homes, educational institutions and other notified silence zones.Violations may lead to confiscation and penal action under applicable laws and Supreme Court directions.The restrictions come as Delhi’s air quality deteriorates ahead of Diwali.A thick layer of smog engulfed the capital on Friday, with the overall Air Quality Index (AQI) touching 391 at 9am, placing it in the ‘very poor’ category and close to the ‘severe’ threshold, PTI reported.Of the 59 monitoring stations across the city, 30 recorded ‘severe’ air quality, while the remaining stations were in the ‘very poor’ category. Rohini recorded the highest AQI at 475, followed by IIT Delhi at 472.According to the Air Quality Early Warning System, Delhi is likely to record its first ‘severe’ air quality day of the season on Friday, with the situation expected to persist until November 8.Firecracker emissions during the festival could add to the existing pollution load, particularly as the period coincides with the peak stubble-burning season in the National Capital Region.The AQI rose from 389 at 8am to 391 at 9am on Friday. The Central Pollution Control Board classifies an AQI of 301-400 as ‘very poor’ and 401-500 as ‘severe’.The Supreme Court on November 2 permitted the manufacture, sale and bursting of approved green firecrackers in Delhi-NCR around Diwali, subject to specified timings.The court also directed that the complete ban on firecrackers be restored from November 9, PTI reported.Separately, the Supreme Court on Friday said vehicular emissions were a major contributor to air pollution in Delhi-NCR and stressed the need for immediate, medium- and long-term measures to bring down pollution levels.The court is scheduled to take up the case again on November 16, after the Diwali vacation.(With agency inputs)
Article Summary: Residents must adhere to specific time slots for bursting firecrackers. The restrictions come as Delhi’s air quality deteriorates ahead of Diwali. A thick layer of smog engulfed the capital on Friday, with the overall Air Quality Index (AQI) touching 391 at 9am.

Article Title: Delhi. Can’t breathe. Can’t move; AQI inches closer to severe; share of farm fires as high as 16.2%
Article Text:
Delhi's air quality index is deteriorating and expected to reach severe levels by Friday (Photo credit: Tarun Rawat)

NCR's best and worst





NEW DELHI: Delhi’s air quality deteriorated further within very poor levels Wednesday, inching closer to the severe category. Local emission sources contributed 31% and external sources 69% to overall air pollution in the city, with the contribution of stubble burning spiking to 16.2% against 8.2% Tuesday.The air quality index (AQI), on a scale of 0 to 500, was 377 against 350 a day earlier at 4pm. The pollution monitoring agencies are anticipating the pollution levels to spike further to severe by Friday.According to IITM’s forecast, the share of pollution from stubble burning in neighbouring states has drastically increased, with Decision Support System’s models predicting the share to rise to 20% by Friday, more than the share of vehicular pollution, which so far had dominated the city’s emission inventory.Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) Wednesday issued show-cause notices over stubble burning to the district commissioners and the SSPs of five districts in Punjab – Barnala, Bathinda, Fazilka, Jalandhar and Faridkot. Officials of Gurdaspur and Kapurthala districts received notices Tuesday.The air quality is likely to be in the very poor category Thursday and in the severe category for around six days from Friday, stated Air Quality Early Warning System by IITM.Despite the GRAP-II restrictions put in place by CAQM Monday and several restrictions already being implemented by Delhi govt since Nov 1 under its new winter pollution framework, AQI in many city areas has already turned severe.Under Delhi govt’s new anti-pollution framework, private construction has been banned from Nov 1 to Jan 31, with a blanket ban between Dec 10 and Jan 20. It has also banned the entry of non-Delhi-registered BS-IV or below vehicles under GRAP-II.Among the areas that slipped into severe levels were IIT Delhi with an AQI of 455, Jahangirpuri 449, Punjabi Bagh 446, Mundka 439, Vivek Vihar 436, DTU 434, Rohini 432, Narela and Alipur 429, Sonia Vihar 427, Pusa 426, RK Puram 424, Bawana 417, Dr Karni Singh Shooting Range, Siri Fort, North Campus and Patparganj 412, and ITO 411.“While transport remains the top local polluter, the spike has been intensified by regional farm fires surging during the last few days, pushing stubble smoke’s contribution to over 8 to 11%. Trapped local emissions and weather stagnation drive this crisis, with farm fires acting as a serious add-on,” said Anumita Roychowdhury, executive director of CSE.The city saw a hazy and partly cloudy sky Wednesday, with the Met department expecting shallow fog and mist Thursday morning. The maximum temperature at base station Safdarjung was 29.8 degrees Celsius, a notch below normal, against 29.1 degrees Celsius a day earlier.The minimum temperature was 16.1 degrees Celsius, a notch above normal, against 16.4 a day earlier.Maximum and minimum temperatures are to hover between 27-29 and 14-17 degrees Celsius Thursday.
Article Summary: The air quality index (AQI), on a scale of 0 to 500, was 377 against 350 a day earlier at 4pm. Pollution monitoring agencies are anticipating the pollution levels to spike further to severe by Friday. Local emission sources contributed 31% and external sources 69% to overall air pollution in the city.

Article Title: How Hyderabad-linked call centre targeted 20 lakh Americans
Article Text:
A call centre fraud network linked to Hyderabad targeted nearly 20 lakh Americans through deceitful practices

Global Network

How the fraud operated

Cash, gold collected from victims

Crypto, hawala trail





HYDERABAD: A Hyderabad-linked call centre fraud network allegedly targeted nearly 20 lakh Americans, many of them elderly, using fake law enforcement threats and scam alerts, while an overseas collection network picked up cash and gold directly from victims’ homes, Enforcement Directorate (ED) stated.ED, which arrested four more accused Wednesday, said its probe uncovered a transnational network spanning India, the US, Dubai and Hong Kong, with proceeds allegedly routed through cryptocurrency channels, mule accounts and hawala operators before being brought into India.The investigation began with the Madhapur call centre case in Hyderabad and subsequently led to the busting of operational call centres in Chandigarh, Patiala and Pune.The scale of the operation emerged from WhatsApp groups recovered during the investigation. ED said the groups recorded 927 approved collections worth $27.39 million (Rs 261 crore) between July 2025 and Sept 2026.According to ED, fraudsters procured databases containing nearly 20 lakh telephone numbers, names, addresses and ages of US residents, many of them senior citizens.The data was fed into auto diallers hosted on servers in Germany and Finland.Preliminary findings indicated the personal information may have been sourced from the dark web and other online platforms.Forensic analysis of seized devices so far identified 549 American victims and targets who had already lost their life savings. Many were born in the 1940s.Investigators said these victims represented only a small fraction of the much larger pool of potential targets contained in the lead databases.The scam typically began with a fake purchase notification, a refund offer, or an alert about a computer virus. Victims were either persuaded to call a toll-free helpline or received calls that appeared to originate from US numbers.Inside the call centres, employees were assigned specific roles. According to ED, “diallers” made the initial contact; “bankers” assessed victims’ financial holdings, and “closers” posed as US govt officials to extract money from them.Callers impersonated officials from drug enforcement administration, department of justice, Federal Trade Commission and US Treasury.To bolster their claims, they allegedly used forged badges, identity cards, seizure notices and court orders, falsely linking victims’ bank accounts to drug trafficking or money laundering cases.To prevent arrest or freezing of their savings, victims were allegedly instructed to maintain secrecy and surrender their money for supposed govt safekeeping.The operation extended beyond telephone calls. ED said US-based associates were deployed to collect cash and gold directly from victims’ homes, while others received parcels through courier stores.Victims were allegedly instructed to purchase gold bars, conceal cash in courier packages, transfer funds to designated accounts, buy gift cards or deposit money through Bitcoin ATMs.Investigators said arrested accused Jaswant Singh coordinated cash pickups and parcel collections in the US and helped route the proceeds into channels that eventually converted them into rupees.Sleuths also recovered Social Security details of 140 Americans along with personal and banking information. ED alleged that identity documents were misused to receive parcels in other people’s names and to create front entities to receive money.Cryptocurrency was used both to move illicit proceeds and to fund the infrastructure needed to run the fraud network, ED alleged.Lead databases, internet-calling services and dialler systems were allegedly paid for using USDT.The money trail ran through US mule accounts, companies in Dubai and Hong Kong, cryptocurrency wallets, and hawala and angadia channels before reaching India.ED said the proceeds were subsequently invested in properties, gold, vehicles, and businesses.Meanwhile, ED’s Hyderabad zonal office continued tracing additional beneficiaries and identifying remaining proceeds of crime.
Article Summary: ED said its probe uncovered a transnational network spanning India, the US, Dubai and Hong Kong. Proceeds allegedly routed through cryptocurrency channels, mule accounts and hawala operators before being brought into India. ED said US- based associates were deployed to collect cash and gold directly from victims’ homes.

Article Title: As $2.5 trillion wiped off Nasdaq in one day, Nvidia and other technology companies that were the biggest losers
Article Text:
Representative image

Nvidia, AMD and semiconductor stocks suffer major losses

Why are investors worried about AI data centres

The Nasdaq 100 index erased $2.5 trillion in market value in a single day as Nvidia and other major technology companies suffered steep losses amid growing fears over the future of artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure spending in the US. According to a Reuters report, the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite plunged 5.5% on November 5, marking its biggest one-day drop since the market sell-off triggered by US President Donald Trump’s “Liberation Day” tariffs in April 2025. The sharp decline came after Democrats scored major victories in the US midterm elections, raising concerns that increased political scrutiny and opposition to data centre construction could slow the expansion of AI infrastructure.Nvidia shares dropped 9% during Thursday’s trading session, while Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) plunged 17%. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index, which tracks major chipmakers, fell 12% and touched its lowest level in more than six months.Several companies directly exposed to AI data centre construction also recorded steep losses. CoreWeave shares fell 10%, while Nebius dropped 15%. Both companies have faced investor concerns over their reliance on borrowing and large-scale infrastructure investments.Data centre operators Applied Digital, Cipher Digital and IREN each tumbled more than 14%. The weakness also extended to companies supplying power and equipment for the AI infrastructure boom. GE Vernova shares fell 7.4%, while Constellation Energy declined 2.5%. Microsoft shares dropped 3.6%, while Amazon and Alphabet each fell 2.2%.As stated in the Reuters report, the Democrats’ strong performance in the US midterm elections has raised concerns that local opposition and tighter scrutiny could slow the construction of new data centres. Several incoming Democratic governors, including in Texas, have called for an immediate moratorium on data centre development.Data centres require large amounts of electricity and water, raising concerns among communities about pressure on power grids and local resources. UBS analysts estimated that around 30% of expected US data centre capacity additions in 2028 could be at risk from potential construction pauses.The latest market downturn also comes as investors question whether the enormous spending on AI infrastructure will deliver adequate returns. Analysts have warned that the AI boom may be entering a phase where companies are judged not just on their growth potential but also on the cost of building and operating their infrastructure. “The market’s moving from the promise of AI to the price of AI,” said Ted Parkhill, founder and CEO of Incline Investment Management as quoted by the news agency.
Article Summary: Nvidia shares dropped 9% during Thursday’s trading session, while Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) plunged 17%. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index, which tracks major chipmakers, fell 12% and touched its lowest level in more than six months. Data centre operators Applied Digital, Cipher Digital and IREN each tumbled more than 14%.

Article Title: Jamie Dimon said on CLARITY Act allowing yield-paying stablecoins that JP Morgan will fight it, if we lose, we lose; here's how Democrat win means end of ...
Article Text:
JP Morgan CEO Jamie Dimon

Jamie Dimon’s warning on CLARITY Act

The bank-crypto fight

Democratic sweep

Greater scrutiny expected for crypto sector

Crypto products expected to keep expanding

The cryptocurrency industry's efforts to secure a comprehensive US regulatory framework could face a major setback after Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress in the midterm elections, with analysts warning that the long-debated CLARITY Act may struggle to advance. The development comes months after JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon vowed to fight provisions that could allow yield-paying stablecoins, arguing that such products pose risks similar to those seen in shadow banking. According to a CoinDesk report, several industry observers believe the Democratic victory has significantly reduced the chances of the CLARITY Act passing in its current form. Mati Greenspan, founder of Quantum Economics, described the Democratic sweep as potentially "the final nail in the CLARITY Act's coffin," noting that the legislation failed to clear a procedural Senate vote even when Republicans controlled both chambers. He said the crypto sector may now have to restart negotiations under a new political landscape.In a Fox Business interview reported by The Globe and Mail in July, Dimon sharpened his criticism of the Digital Asset Market Clarity (CLARITY) Act, saying he feared yield-paying stablecoins could cause a “shadow banking” crisis. “We’ll fight it. If we lose, we lose, and we’ll live,” he said. Dimon argues that such tokens are effectively unregulated deposit-like products.Without capital requirements, he says, they could destabilise markets in a way similar to shadow banking in the 2008 financial crisis. In May, Dimon criticised Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong in a Fox Business interview, according to Bloomberg, using crude language to dismiss him. He said banks “will not accept” the current version of the bill.The CLARITY Act, intended to set a federal framework for digital assets, passed the House last year. It stalled in the Senate over whether crypto firms can pay yield on stablecoins. A compromise reached in May would ban passive rewards earned simply by holding tokens, but allow activity-based rewards tied to transactions or platform use.Coinbase and other exchanges back yield-bearing stablecoins, arguing they expand consumer choice and innovation. Banks, led by Dimon and the American Bankers Association, want them banned outright to protect deposits and financial stability. A ban would hit Circle, issuer of the USDC stablecoin, which earns interest on the cash and Treasuries backing its tokens, and Coinbase, which shares in Circle’s reserve income and earns fees from stablecoin trading.CoinDesk reported that the crypto industry’s hopes for a regulatory framework took another blow when Democrats won both chambers. “For crypto, the Democratic sweep may well be the final nail in the Clarity Act’s coffin,” said Mati Greenspan, founder of Quantum Economics. He noted the bill couldn’t even clear a procedural vote in September, when Republicans controlled both chambers, and that the industry may now have to start from scratch in a divided Washington.Stefan Muehlbauer, head of US government affairs at CertiK, said the bill is likely dead in its current form. Anton Golub said crypto political action groups spent about $170.5 million on the elections, with at least $125.5 million going to Republicans. Despite Republican control of Congress and a crypto-friendly President Donald Trump, the bill failed to advance in September. Golub said Trump made regulators friendlier to the industry, but his family’s crypto involvement also gave Democrats a reason to oppose crypto-friendly legislation.Several industry participants expect Democrats to take a more aggressive approach toward crypto oversight. CoinDesk reported that lawmakers could focus on issues including anti-money laundering controls, cybersecurity practices and consumer protection measures.Muehlbauer said congressional hearings and investigations may examine both cryptocurrency companies and President Trump's crypto-related business interests. Meanwhile, Shady El Damaty, co-founder of Human.tech, predicted increased scrutiny of tokenised stock offerings and broader crypto expansion efforts by trading platforms.Not everyone believes the legislation is beyond saving. Brent Fulfer, co-founder of venture capital firm TBV, noted that more than 70 House Democrats previously supported the CLARITY Act and argued that a revised bill with stronger safeguards and bipartisan backing could still gain traction.While the regulatory outlook has become more uncertain, some industry executives believe innovation in digital asset products will continue. Golub said products such as perpetual futures are likely to grow beyond cryptocurrencies and expand into equities and other traditional financial markets.Jason Fernandes, founder of AdLunam, said the crypto industry should engage constructively with Democratic lawmakers rather than oppose stricter oversight outright. According to Fernandes, carefully targeted regulation and enforcement against bad actors could ultimately strengthen the broader crypto ecosystem.
Article Summary: Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress in midterm elections. Analysts warn that the long-debated CLARITY Act may struggle to advance. JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon has vowed to fight provisions that could allow yield-paying stablecoins.
